We adopt a shape-driven analysis strategy with a floating overall normalization, so that the discovery power relies on the spectral distortion rather than on the absolute event rate. In a realistic scenario with 90% spallation rejection efficiency, informed by the Super-Kamiokande experience and recent JUNO analyses, residual spallation backgrounds prevent either signal from reaching $5σ$ significance within 20 years of exposure. For the hep flux, we present a detailed sensitivity study to both its discovery and its precision, and quantify how the required spallation veto efficiency and recoil energy threshold jointly determine the achievable significance for both signals. At the adopted thresholds, discovery-level sensitivity for both signals requires approximately 99% spallation rejection over a 20-year exposure.

title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
abstract: We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
abstract: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

title: Global phase-plane organization of a toxin-mediated plant-herbivore model
abstract: Plant-herbivore interactions with chemical plant defence mechanisms can generate complex population dynamics through the nonlinear interplay between resource availability, herbivore pressure, and defence-induced feedbacks. In this work, we investigate the dynamical organization of a plant-herbivore model characterized by a non-monotone functional response accounting for inhibitory effects on grazing activity. In particular, we perform a qualitative and geometric analysis of the associated homogeneous system, characterizing the dynamical regimes supported by the model and the transitions between them. The results reveal the emergence of oscillatory behaviour through a Hopf bifurcation and the occurrence of stable periodic solutions. We further characterize the global phase-plane organization, providing a complete classification of equilibrium configurations and heteroclinic structures supported by the model. In addition, we identify the conditions under which homoclinic connections may occur and discuss their role in shaping the global dynamics. The analysis provides a unified description of the phase-plane organization and highlights how nonlinear defence feedbacks generate qualitatively distinct ecological outcomes, including extinction, stable coexistence, persistent oscillations, and global bifurcation scenarios organized by heteroclinic and homoclinic structures.

title: Horizon mergers and initial test-charge acceleration in charged black-hole geometries with anisotropic sources
abstract: We study horizon mergers and the initial radial acceleration of charged test particles in static, spherically symmetric black-hole geometries with a string cloud, a Kiselev power-law component, or a logarithmic profile conventionally. After separating the Maxwell contribution, the effective environmental stress tensors are anisotropic and are not identified with homogeneous quintessence or pressureless cold dark matter. Using a common mass-function formulation, we derive the horizon-merger conditions and classify the Kiselev branches. In this family, the inner-event merger charge provides only an upper bound: three distinct positive horizons can additionally require a positive lower charge bound associated with the event-cosmological merger. For a test particle released from rest relative to a static observer, we derive the local charge-to-mass threshold for outward initial acceleration. Writing $λ=q/μ$ and $z=Q/Q_{\rm ext}$, where $Q_{\rm ext}$ is the inner-event merger charge, the subextremal string-cloud threshold has infimum $1/z$, approached only at infinity. For the subextremal logarithmic profile, the threshold exceeds unity throughout the finite exterior and attains a finite global minimum. For $α/M=0.4$ and $Q/M=1.2$, this minimum is $λ_*\simeq1.251125$. In a nondegenerate Kiselev static patch, the neutral balance radius is unique and radially unstable. Density matching supplies conditional profile normalizations, not observational fits. For the logarithmic profile, the integration parameter is distinguished from the mass combination inferred from circular motion. These results characterize geometric horizon bounds and test-particle dynamics; they do not establish a two-black-hole force law or a mechanism for cosmic acceleration, nor do they constitute a test of the Weak Gravity Conjecture.

title: Pohlmeyer reduction of Newton-Cartan strings
abstract: We develop a Pohlmeyer-type reduction for classical non-relativistic strings on string Newton-Cartan backgrounds. For strings on a two-sphere, we identify the invariant reduced field, show that its dynamics is integrable, and construct a Lax representation. We relate this intrinsic formulation to the non-relativistic expansion of relativistic strings and obtain a dictionary between non-relativistic string solutions and their reduced counterparts. The construction explicitly determines which relativistic solitonic configurations survive the non-relativistic limit and which decouple. Moreover, it provides a framework for applying integrability methods to Newton-Cartan string dynamics.

title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
abstract: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $η(1405)\toπ^{+}π^{-}π^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $π^+π^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point. These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.

title: Small-ball asymptotics of Gaussian matrix products: Open Fermi shells and the Grassmannian
abstract: Let $P=A_N\cdots A_1$ be a product of independent standard real or complex Gaussian matrices of arbitrary fixed sizes. For complex entries we determine the exact leading terms, of the form $κ\,\varepsilon^C(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$, of the operator-norm and Frobenius small-ball probabilities of $P$, together with the corresponding asymptotics of the Laplace transform of $\|P^2\|_{F}$. The exponent $C$ is the known diversity order, while the logarithmic power follows a filling rule: when fermions are placed on ladders of states determined by the sizes and the last occupied level has degeneracy $μ$ and contains $h$ particles, $q=h(μ-h)$. The determinant of this last shell expands in Plücker coordinates graded by the Schubert cells of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(h,μ)$, with leading coefficients proportional to normalized degrees of Schubert varieties. For real entries we prove that the Frobenius small-ball probability has an exact positive leading term of order $\varepsilon^{C/2}(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$ and that the operator-norm probability has the same order, which gives a proof of the known real log canonical threshold and its multiplicity that needs no explicit resolution of singularities. We evaluate the real leading coefficient in closed form for every shell with at most one logarithm, a class that contains all products of two factors, and we conjecture its general form, which agrees with the classical constant of vector chains. Applications include the outage probability of cascaded multi-antenna channels at high signal-to-noise ratio and the Bayesian evidence of deep linear networks.

title: An energy-dependent rescaling of the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian: Standard Model Extension identification, matter sector, and long-baseline degeneracy
abstract: We study the consequences of multiplying the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian by a real, energy-dependent scalar, $H_η(E)=f(E)H_0(E)$ with $f(E)=1-η_0(E/E_0)^2$, a minimal-length ansatz. Its vacuum part is a dimension-four, CPT-even Lorentz-violating term of the Standard Model Extension with coefficient $(\cL)_{ii}=-η_0(m_i^2-m_1^2)/(2E_0^2)$, diagonal in the mass basis and fixed by the mass matrix, hence removable by a reparametrization. The matter-potential rescaling has dimension-five behaviour and is CPT-odd. For $f=1-η_0(E/E_0)^p$ the vacuum term behaves as a dimension $p+2$ operator and the matter term as $p+3$, so only $p=2$ gives a marginal vacuum operator; $p=0$ is absorbed into the measured mass splittings, and non-integer $p$ admits no local operator. For $η_0=0.02$ at $E_0=2.5$~GeV we find $|(\cL)_{33}|\simeq4\times10^{-24}$, comparable to present atmospheric bounds, whereas a Planck-suppressed deformation with $β_0=\mathcal{O}(1)$ gives $3.2\times10^{-58}$. At constant density it is equivalent to $L\to f(E)L$: mixing angles and the Dirac phase are unchanged, the CP asymmetry is reparametrized rather than generated, and the leading observable is a rescaling of $\dm_{31}$. At $1297$~km a re-fit of $\dm_{31}$ alone absorbs $23$~per cent of the squared probability difference, and a four-parameter re-fit absorbs $41.5$~per cent. No statistical analysis is performed; degeneracy means a distance in probability space, not a confidence interval.

title: Global well-posedness and regularization for a nonlinear relativistic Fokker--Planck equation
abstract: We consider a nonlinear relativistic Fokker--Planck equation on momentum space, whose diffusion coefficient and drift vector field are nonlinear integral functionals of the solution. We prove global existence and uniqueness of weak probability density solutions preserving the relativistic energy-momentum $(E,P)$. A fundamental step in the proof is to establish that the scalar diffusion coefficient remains uniformly positive on every finite time interval. The key mechanism ensuring this property is the strict relativistic inequality $E^2-|P|^2>1$, combined with the uniform integrability of the energy tails on every finite time interval. We further prove that global weak solutions become instantaneously smooth and strictly positive for positive times. Finally, for even initial data, we prove that the diffusion coefficient remains uniformly positive for all time.

title: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
abstract: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordström black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.

title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
abstract: Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,Ω)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[ \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr) [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms. We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.

title: Towards the componentwise three-soliton conjecture: cones, collisions, soft momenta and graphs
abstract: The componentwise three-soliton conjecture of Part~I states that if an even polynomial $P$ with $P(0)=0$ satisfies Hirota's three-soliton condition on a non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one of its dispersion variety, then it satisfies the $N$-soliton condition there for every $N$. We prove restrictions on components carrying this condition and classify the polynomials satisfying it on several families of components, with no degree bound. Restrictions: if the top homogeneous part of the equation of the component has a nonlinear irreducible factor, then $P$ is a multiple of a quadratic form; the order of $P$ at the origin is tied to the multiplicities of the component and of the doubled component; a component through the origin has odd multiplicity; the condition passes to all limits of the rescaled component, and the Newton polygon of a plane component has edges of only ten directions. Classifications: on the cubic graph $v=u^3$, where the four-soliton condition holds exactly in multiplicity one; on the graphs $v=q(u)$ with $°q\ge3$, where $P$ exists only if $q$ is an odd cubic or an odd quintic, so the conjecture holds for all graphs of polynomials; and for three families of Hietarinta's list, where each irreducible member is, up to a constant factor, the only such polynomial on its dispersion variety. All three satisfy the $N$-soliton condition for every $N$, so the conjecture holds for them: two belong to the BKP hierarchy, and for Hietarinta's quartic equation, known to satisfy it for $N\le4$, we prove it by fusing resonant momenta and counting zeros on its curve. For translated hyperbolas we exclude the one through the origin and all $P$ of degree at most eight. The solutions of multiplicity one on graphs are known bilinear equations; new is that there are no others. The conjecture remains open.

title: A Brownian web invariance principle: Localized disturbance flows and Hastings-Levitov(0)
abstract: We establish a Brownian web invariance principle for localized disturbance flows, providing a criterion that strengthens the weak-flow convergence of [Norris--Turner 2015, Ann. Probab. 43, 935--970] to path-Hausdorff convergence of their full trajectory collections. We apply this approach to the radial, stationary, and cylindrical versions of the Hastings--Levitov$(0)$ aggregation model, proving path-Hausdorff convergence of the full harmonic measure path collections to the (Cylindrical) Brownian web, together with joint convergence of the full gap--finger collections to geometric embeddings of the corresponding double Brownian webs. This extends the radial HL$(0)$ small-particle limits of [Norris--Turner 2012, Commun. Math. Phys. 316, 809--841] for the harmonic measure flow and finite gap--finger collections. In the radial and cylindrical HL$(0)$, we also show that the rescaled one-arm domination time converges to a multiple of the global coalescence time of coalescing Brownian motion on $\mathbb T$, with convergence of expectations. The main new ingredient is a three-point survival estimate, proved via a multiscale stopping-time decomposition.

title: Regge bounds and eikonal estimates in scalar effective field theory
abstract: Positivity bounds are derived from twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which hold only if the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partialφ)^4/Λ^4$ and $g_6(\partialφ)^6/Λ^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. Matching the two regions gives the phase-model growth $s^{8/7}$ for the quartic sector and $s^{16/15}$ for the sextic sector, while a transition scale fixed by the cutoff gives the conditional bound $s^{7/4}$; in the forward limit the same construction gives only the marginal growth $s^2$, so that Regge boundedness remains an assumption on the completion. Under this assumption the $2\to 2$ and $2\to 4$ absorptive parts below the cutoff restrict the couplings to $0<g_4\le 80π^2/7$ and $-7.2\times 10^5\lesssim g_6\lesssim 6.9\times 10^5$.

title: Regular/Singular Black Hole Thermodynamics from Renormalised Volume/Area
abstract: We study the finite mismatch between the holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions of the four-dimensional AdS C-metric. Starting from the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity, we separate the regular curvature contribution from the contributions supported on the two conical axes. After introducing the usual Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds, the residual difference between the regular action evaluations is determined by the tension-weighted Euler terms of the renormalised worldsheet area. We identify this difference with the Gauss--Bonnet entropy contribution at the polar conical points of the horizon. The ordinary Euler characteristic remains fixed, while the deficits determine how its curvature representation is divided between regular and singular contributions. At fixed total string tension, the difference of the renormalised worldsheet areas per unit Euclidean time determines the relative tension work, giving a geometric interpretation of the relative thermodynamic length.

title: Search for the low-mass isotropic signature of QCD instantons in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV using the ATLAS detector
abstract: This Letter presents the first search for QCD instanton-induced events at the LHC. Instantons are semi-classical solutions of the Yang-Mills equations of QCD and correspond to non-perturbative tunneling between topologically distinct vacuum sectors. The search is performed in 1.6 $\text{nb}^{-1}$ of very low instantaneous luminosity proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector at 13 TeV. Angular variables based on reconstructed charged-particle tracks are used to discriminate the expected rest-frame isotropy of low-mass instanton events from the minimum-bias background. The minimum-bias event background is predicted using a data-driven technique and reweighted Monte Carlo models. A profile-likelihood fit is performed in a two-dimensional classifier variable to extract a possible signal contribution, yielding an excess of low-mass isotropic events with an observed significance of $3.5σ$.

title: A no-go theorem for closed timelike curves in globally null-foliated spacetimes
abstract: The study of closed timelike curves has proceeded one spacetime at a time, and the criteria available form three families, the time function criteria, the energy condition criteria and the topological criteria. We initiate a fourth family of criteria, elementary in form and resting on a single scalar equation rather than any energy condition. We prove that a spacetime admitting a globally defined function whose gradient is everywhere null and nonzero cannot contain a closed timelike curve, and that the hypothesis is logically independent of stable causality rather than weaker than it. The proof turns on one algebraic fact, that a null covector is never orthogonal to a timelike vector, so the function grows strictly along every timelike curve and cannot close. Because the null eikonal equation alone decides the criterion, we can use it where the classical time function theorem is silent. We establish for the first time that no Kundt spacetime and no Robinson--Trautman spacetime can contain a closed timelike curve on any region where the null coordinate is globally single valued, whatever the cosmological constant and the rotation one form, which settles a question left open for gyratonic waves. We further show that the Misner, Ori and Ahmed constructions contain closed timelike curves along coordinate circles that become timelike under the periodic identification, and that the cosmological constant, the expansion and the shear are spectators in all of them.

title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
abstract: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored. Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others. The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.

title: Landau-Ginzburg Theory of a Holographic Superconductor: A Horizon Perspective on the Zero-Temperature Ground State
abstract: We investigate the effect of a quartic scalar self-interaction, $λ|φ|^4$, on a holographic superconductor in which non-linear electrodynamic couplings generate a superconducting dome containing an extended Lifshitz regime. The quartic interaction leaves the linearized scalar dynamics around the normal phase unchanged while modifying the non-linear solutions where the scalar field is large. As $λ$ increases, the solutions within the dome pass through three stages. The Lifshitz region shrinks until its scaling solution disappears at $λ^*$, leaving a no-AdS region, beyond whose edge the flows end before reaching any asymptotic region, and above $λ_c$ the dome consists entirely of asymptotically AdS hairy black holes. At the bottom of the dome we identify the point where the horizon value of the scalar field is largest, which we refer to as the critical point. There this value lies at the deepest symmetry-breaking minimum that the horizon effective potential, of Landau-Ginzburg form, can have. Unlike a conventional Landau-Ginzburg description, this interpretation rests on the scalar field at the horizon rather than on the boundary order parameter. Below $λ^*$, the constant scalar of the Lifshitz fixed point sits instead at the minimum of the effective potential of its asymptotic scaling region.

title: Near-horizon BF bounds for the $t^+$ KK tower on extremal AdS$_5$ black holes
abstract: We study the charged Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound for all horizon harmonics of the type IIB $t^+$ Kaluza--Klein tower on extremal charged AdS$_5$ black holes with equal rotations. The scalar equation follows from maximal five-dimensional gauged supergravity at level zero and the linearized exceptional-field-theory equations at higher levels. For aligned charge and rotation, a quadratic form in charge and spin changes signature on the curve of supersymmetric (BPS) black holes, where every mode satisfies the bound. Above the curve, where $Ω_H>1$, every black hole has a violating mode, although no finite truncation in level or spin detects violation at every such black hole. Below the curve, where $Φ_H>1$, the BF-passing set is confined to a thin strip and controlled by charge and spin discreteness. At large radius and fixed rotation, a level-four mode with spin proportional to the radius violates the bound even where all U(2) singlets satisfy it. These results concern the near-horizon BF bound of one tower in two-derivative supergravity; full radial stability remains open.

title: Orbital Stability and Instability of Slow and Fast Solitary Waves of gILW
abstract: We study the solitary waves of the generalized Intermediate Long Wave equation (gILW), for a power-type nonlinearity of order $p\geq1$. Using concentration-compactness and symmetric rearrangement, we prove existence of suitable (even, strictly positive and radially decreasing) solitary waves of gILW for every $p\geq1$, and show that, as the depth parameter tends to infinity, they converge in the energy space and in $L^q$, $q\in[2,\infty]$, to the solitary waves of the generalized Benjamin-Ono equation (gBO), while, as the depth parameter tends to zero, after a suitable rescaling, they converge in $L^q$, $q\in[2,\infty]$, to the solitary waves of the generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation (gKdV). Our main results concern the orbital stability of slow and fast solitary waves of gILW, that is, of those for which the product $δc$ of the depth parameter and the velocity is small or large, respectively. For slow waves we obtain stability for $p=1,2,3$ and instability for $p\geq5$ (the same threshold as for gKdV), while for fast waves we obtain stability for $p=1$ and instability for $p\geq3$ (the same threshold as for gBO). In particular, for $p=3$ the stability of the solitary waves changes from one regime to the other. These results extend to $p>1$ the classical result of Albert, Bona and Henry for the Intermediate Long Wave equation ($p=1$). The proof proceeds by perturbation theory, transferring spectral information from gKdV and gBO to gILW through the convergence of the corresponding solitary-wave operators, and in particular avoids any use of an explicit formula for the solitary wave profile, none being available for $p>1$.

title: The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
abstract: We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $ρ$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2πρ(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ))$ as $ρ\to 0$, and the condensate fraction $η$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $η= 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ)$ as $ρ\to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case. The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,χ_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.

title: Covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus, non-dissipative transport and the chiral anomaly in inhomogeneous systems with nontrivial momentum-space topology
abstract: We review, systematize and extend the covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus for fermions in non-Abelian gauge fields and its applications to systems inhomogeneous in coordinate space with nontrivial momentum-space topology: the non-Abelian chiral separation and quantum Hall effects, their stability under interactions, the Fermi-surface invariant of inhomogeneous systems and the non-elliptic models that carry it, the factorization of the chiral anomaly into the instanton number and the momentum-space invariant $N_3$, and the noncommutative-geometric form of the invariants.

title: A refined upper bound on the critical temperature for dilute Bose gases
abstract: We establish an upper bound on the critical temperature shift of three-dimensional Bose gases with general nonnegative finite-range interactions. In the dilute regime $aρ^{1/3}\to0$, we prove $T_c(ρ)/T_c^{(0)}(ρ) \le 1 + (C_{\rm H}+o(1))\sqrt{aρ^{1/3}}$, where \[ C_{\rm H}=\frac{2^{7/2}\sqrtπ}{3ζ(3/2)^{2/3}} =3.523992\ldots \] is the coefficient predicted by Huang in 1999. This improves the earlier rigorous upper bound of Seiringer and Ueltschi in 2009. More precisely, we prove the exponential decay of the correlations above the stated temperature through the Feynman--Kac representation, for both integrable and hard-core interactions.

title: A Geometric Framework for Local-to-Global Symmetry: Global Constraints on Local Dynamics
abstract: Aggregate molecular systems are routinely understood by decomposing them into local structural units, such as monomers in J/H-aggregates, chemical moieties, motifs, and functional groups. Implicit in such decompositions is the assumption that these local structures remain meaningful within the aggregate. Here, we ask how the symmetries of constituent structures relate to aggregate symmetry, and how this relation determines the constraints that global symmetry imposes on transitions between local symmetry sectors. We construct a covariant local-to-global representation from framed local symmetry data and show that its reconstruction map intertwines with a global quantum representation. By identifying which global symmetry sectors overlap each local symmetry sector, we resolve symmetry-enforced dynamical exclusions into site-resolved pathways. Through Frobenius reciprocity, these exclusions can be determined from standard character tables of the local and global symmetry groups, with the character values in the inner product paired according to the relative positions and orientations of local structures within the aggregate. Although motivated by molecular aggregates, the construction is formulated for arbitrary geometries modeled by a homogeneous space of an ambient transformation group.

title: Linearization of nonlocal elasticity based on nonlocal gradients via Γ-convergence
abstract: We provide a rigorous variational derivation of linear nonlocal elasticity from a general nonlinear elastic model based on nonlocal gradients. Under standard assumptions of nonlinear elasticity, we prove that the rescaled nonlinear energies Γ-converge, in the small-strain limit, to the corresponding quadratic linearized energy. The proof relies on a nonlocal geometric rigidity estimate and does not require any global upper growth condition on the stored-energy density.

title: Anomaly inflow for simplicial Kähler fermions
abstract: We study massive Kähler Dirac fermions propagating on finite triangulations of various three dimensional manifolds with one or more boundaries. To probe the anomaly structure of these models we decompose the Kähler field into two reduced Kähler fields and choose boundary conditions that ensure that any edge modes are necessarily massless. We then show how to factorize the Pfaffian of this system into a product of bulk and boundary sectors each of which can separately pick up a phase under a global $Z_4$ transformation of the fermions that simultaneously changes the sign of the mass. These phases are topological, depending only on the index of the lattice Kähler operator in that sector. For the boundary sector a non-trivial phase signals the presence of a 't Hooft anomaly. We study cases where the boundary is anomalous but an inflow from the bulk cancels its phase. Canceling this anomaly for a non-orientable boundary in the absence of the bulk recovers the known classification of topological superconductors. We also give a continuum interpretation of these results in terms of inflow from a gravitational Chern Simons theory which is induced by integrating out massive bulk Kähler Dirac fermions. In the presence of a boundary the latter gives rise to Wen-Zee terms that mediate the anomaly inflow mechanism.

title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
abstract: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. Our results span weak to strong coupling, reproduce the known perturbative and string-theory limits, and are consistent with conformal-bootstrap bounds. We also obtain new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients and extract new strong-coupling data from high-precision numerical fits.

title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in $2+1$ Dimensions
abstract: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions. In a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a $\mathbb Z_2\times O(n)$ scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous $O(n)$ symmetry at finite temperatures. Nevertheless, for $n=2$, a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless superfluid phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures. In this phase, spatial correlations decay algebraically, with an exponent that approaches zero as the temperature increases. For $n\geq 3$, we uncover a further unexpected feature of these models: the characteristic size of ordered domains grows asymptotically with temperature, revealing an unusual enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating. We establish our results using a controlled high-temperature expansion, with selected findings corroborated by numerical functional renormalization group analysis. The simplicity of the field content in these models provides a promising starting point for exploring experimental realizations of persistent thermal order in thin-film materials.

title: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices
abstract: We investigate how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation shape vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. At fixed lattice spacing and finite geometry, we establish that logarithmic negativity remains uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges. Infrared-enhanced total correlations therefore do not provide an unbounded distillable-entanglement resource. Using local symplectic consolidation, we identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and follow their evolution with separation. Their participation crosses over from localization near the facing boundaries to a collective distribution within each region. Expansion in the adjacent-state canonical basis connects this evolution to progressively weaker, more extended reference modes, including adjacent-halo directions. Building on the established concentration of long-distance logarithmic negativity into a single canonical pair, we show that its spatial participation is smooth and infrared-dominated despite its ultraviolet canonical structure, a distinction also present in pure-state entanglement modes. These results refine the ultraviolet mode picture by resolving the long-wavelength organization of the oscillators participating in the surviving entanglement. Across the massless dispersions studied, the normalized participation approaches a universal long-distance profile when separation is scaled by the negativity radius. Its detailed form and the entanglement range nevertheless remain sensitive to ultraviolet deformations. Together, these findings distinguish infrared-enhanced correlations from distillable entanglement and reveal the collective spatial organization underlying its persistence at large separation.

title: Hill's Lunar Equation as a Leaf: Riccati Reduction and Frobenius Theory for Second-Order PDEs
abstract: The equations of Hill and Adams for the lunar perigee and node, Mathieu's equation and Lamé's equation arise as leafwise restrictions of one class of linear partial differential equations, the \emph{square-type foliated equations} $L^2u+A\,Lu+B\,u=0$, where $L$ is an analytic vector field and $A,B$ are analytic functions. Such an equation has a regular singularity exactly when the foliation defined by $L$ is analytically linearizable. At rational saddles, where every point of the indicial conic is resonant, we obtain convergent solutions whose exponents are holomorphic functions of a first integral; their variation describes the monodromy along the leaves and decides when classical Frobenius solutions exist. For a Hill equation, the characteristic exponent becomes the value of such a holomorphic function, given by a convergent series. This yields rigorous computer-assisted proofs of Hill's constant for the motion of the lunar perigee and of Adams' constant for the motion of the node: Hill's value is confirmed within his own error estimate and its fifteenth decimal is determined, his value of the motion of the perigee is shown to be correct in all its digits, and Adams' value is confirmed to twelve decimals. For Mathieu's equation, the curves of constant characteristic exponent that govern ion trapping appear as classical Frobenius loci. For Lamé's equation, we prove a product formula for the logarithmic obstructions, which coincide with the leading coefficients of the eigenvalue splittings computed by Volkmer and whose vanishing reflects the finite-gap property.

title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $τ^+τ^-$ production through $μ^+μ^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $τ$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $μ^+μ^-\toτ^+τ^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|Δa_τ|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
abstract: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.

title: Hidden convexity of the Eliashberg condensation energy: existence, uniqueness and continuity of the superconducting state
abstract: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables $ρ_n=\sin^2θ_n$, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted $\ell^1$ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the $γ$-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separately established spectral input. Finite-dimensional algebraic and convex-analytic components are machine-checked in Lean. The proofs were obtained independently of concurrent work that reaches overlapping conclusions.

title: Training for sustainable scientific software in the AI era: from code production to scientific stewardship
abstract: Generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are changing how researchers interact with scientific software. Their effects on productivity vary across tasks and users, but they can weaken the connection between producing a successful computational artifact and retaining scientific command over the consequential choices and evidence on which it depends. For high-energy physics, this shifts part of the training challenge from code production toward scientific stewardship: researchers must be able to validate, explain, reproduce, maintain, and justify software and workflows partly generated or modified by AI. We argue that AI-aware software training should therefore combine dedicated instruction on AI systems with the integration of AI into established software and analysis training. Testing, provenance, reproducibility, resource judgment, and scientific validation should be exercised in AI-assisted workflows, with competence judged by the evidence supporting a result rather than by code generation alone. We frame this as a problem of sustainable scientific software: AI-assisted workflows should remain trustworthy and maintainable, use computational resources responsibly, and avoid making core competence unnecessarily dependent on privileged access to particular tools or infrastructure.

title: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory
abstract: As a consequence of the relativistic spectrum condition, quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space are never described by projection-valued measures, and in many cases fail a weaker spacetime localisation property known as the norm-$1$ condition. This has several implications for the local and observable structure of quantum field theories described relative to even the best available frame: for a large class of frame states, strict locality is replaced by almost locality, and microcausality by commutators that decay rapidly with increasing separation, corresponding to an effective smearing of the light cone by the localisation density of the frame state. Operations built from finitely many almost local Kraus operators, for example nonselective measurements of relativised local observables, satisfy an approximate no-signalling bound, with a residue attributable to the localisation uncertainty of the frame. Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.

title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high even dimensions
abstract: We prove that the spherically symmetric $SO(d)$ Yang--Mills equation admits a third smooth self-similar profile, in addition to the two known explicit profiles, in every even dimension $d\geq 12$. This complements the analogous existence theorem in odd dimensions $d\geq 11$ (arXiv:2610.36784). In contrast to the odd-dimensional case, where the classification of smooth self-similar profiles reduces to counting roots of an explicit resonance polynomial [Phys. Rev. D 114, 064021 (2026)], the even-dimensional proof requires solving a nonlinear connection problem. In $d=10$, where one explicit profile degenerates to the zero solution, we give a formal argument for the existence of a second nontrivial smooth profile in addition to the single nontrivial explicit one.

title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.

title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
abstract: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.

title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
abstract: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm iβ/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.

title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
abstract: Standard Model fermion masses exhibit large hierarchies, spanning more than five orders of magnitude in the quark sector alone. In this paper, we study whether these hierarchies can be generated perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, where the supergravity approximation remains under computational control. In such backgrounds, physical Yukawa couplings combine holomorphic superpotential integrals with matter field Kahler metrics. The former can be computed algebraically, while the latter require solving a coupled system of partial differential equations for the Ricci-flat metric, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms. Within this framework, we identify two new tree-level mechanisms by which complex structure moduli can generate fermion mass hierarchies and show analytically and numerically that both mechanisms are obstructed for previously studied tetra-quadric models. Motivated by these obstructions, we scan the existing databases of tens of thousands of complete intersection Calabi-Yau line bundle models and find a unique smooth quotient admitting a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix at tree level. Evaluating the physical couplings on this manifold and evolving them under the renormalization group, we obtain realistic mass hierarchies for the top, charm, up, and bottom quarks in the smooth supergravity regime.

title: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability
abstract: Whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system with geometrically local, bounded-degree interactions can passively protect encoded quantum information has remained a central open question since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Passive protection requires stability against both thermal noise at nonzero temperature and generic static Hamiltonian perturbations Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) recently established unperturbed three-dimensional thermal self-correction using a recursively defined family of stabilizer Hamiltonians. However, they left open whether their construction remains stable against quantum perturbations, even at zero temperature. In this paper, we show that a slight variant of the BDL code family achieves stability along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as the system size grows. Following BDL, in the absence of perturbation it is thermally stable below a critical temperature, achieving a stretched-exponentially long memory lifetime when coupled to any local Markovian thermal bath generated by single-site system-bath interactions satisfying detailed balance with bounded coupling rates. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, the family maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap, superpolynomially small ground-space splitting, and a superpolynomially long closed-system unitary memory lifetime for quasi-locally dressed logical observables. To prove this zero-temperature stability, we establish local topological quantum order across the multiscale hierarchy using a linearly dilated relaxation of the usual Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis criteria. In the companion paper, we combine the tools developed here with finite-temperature worldline cluster expansions to establish passive self-correction throughout the phase diagram's positive-temperature perturbed interior.

title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
abstract: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $θ=π$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.

title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
abstract: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal Čech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.

title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.

title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
abstract: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlevé V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.

title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
abstract: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.

title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
abstract: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;α)$ factor.

title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
abstract: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2π$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).

title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
abstract: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $π^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $π^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $π^\pm$-$π^0$ mass splitting.

title: Not All Holographic Entropy Inequalities Are Free of Area Law Ultraviolet Divergences
abstract: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, linear constraints on subsystem entropies, which are necessary conditions for the validity of the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal, define the holographic entropy cone. We disprove a prior claim that all holographic constraints of this type are free of area law divergences (superbalanced). We analyze one explicit counterexample and explain how to easily find more; we report signatures of $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ counterexamples. Our findings invalidate multiple prior claims and conjectures.

title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
abstract: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.

title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding
abstract: The python's lunch conjecture relates the complexity of bulk reconstruction in holographic tensor networks to an exponential cost associated with post-selection. We establish a tight query lower bound for this decoding problem in a Haar random oracle model, with a python's lunch circuit that applies Haar random unitary $U$ to a logical input and fixed ancillas, followed by post-selection on $m$ output qubits. Given one copy of the normalized encoded state and coherent oracle access to $U$ and $U^\dagger$, including controlled queries, we prove that recovering even a single logical bit with constant average advantage requires $Ω(2^{m/2})$ queries. Together with the state-independent amplitude amplification upper bound for approximately isometric encodings, this establishes query complexity $Θ(2^{m/2})$ at constant decoding accuracy. We also comment on the decoding cost for other "admissible'" ensembles of unitaries $U$ which give rise to families of approximately isometric holographic maps.

title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity
abstract: Integrating Euclidean semiclassical gravity over real Riemannian metrics is subtle due to the conformal factor problem. A perturbative prescription was given by Gibbons-Hawking-Perry (GHP) where the integration contour for the conformal perturbations is rotated to be imaginary. A potential non-perturbative remedy is that the integration cycles associated to semiclassical saddle points should be deformed into the space of complex metrics in the sense of Picard-Lefschetz theory. Here we propose a non-perturbative construction of such complex integration cycles. This employs a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, starting at a saddle point, along which the action has monotonically increasing real part and constant imaginary part. The flow is not parabolic. In a neighbourhood of a saddle point, the real part of the conformal factor flows forward and that of the conformal class backwards, with the opposite true of their imaginary parts. Starting the flow at a saddle point, then roughly speaking, one specifies the real part of the conformal class and the imaginary part of the conformal factor at the end of the flow. Solving the flow one finds the complex metrics along a one parameter path within the integration cycle of that saddle, and varying this final data generates the integration cycle, the Lefschetz thimble of the saddle point. We find that near to a real saddle point this reproduces the GHP prescription. We characterise the neighbourhood of a saddle where such forward-backward flows may exist, finding a weaker restriction than that of Kontsevich-Segal-Witten. We numerically demonstrate flows explicitly for 4-dimensional gravity, constructing sections through the integration contours for the saddles given by Euclidean de Sitter, and for Schwarzschild in a cavity.

title: An infrared-safe $S$-matrix for $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills
abstract: Scattering amplitudes of massless gauge theories are not observables: they are infrared divergent, and the standard regulators are tied either to perturbation theory or the planar limit. We study $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory on rigid AdS$_4$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the role of the amplitude is played by correlation functions of boundary operators. These are finite, and they are defined at any coupling and for any gauge group. Among them, the four-point function of the flavor-current supermultiplet is the counterpart of the $2\to2$ amplitude of the elementary supergluon states, and arguably the simplest non-trivial observable of the theory. In this paper, we compute it at weak coupling to one loop. The tree-level correlator follows directly from the microscopic theory, and the one-loop correlator, which we obtain from AdS unitarity, takes a remarkably simple form in Mellin space. In the flat-space limit, it reproduces the one-loop scattering amplitude, with the infrared divergences re-emerging as logarithms.

title: Isomorphisms of Class S Theories with IndexLab
abstract: We use IndexLab to scan untwisted and twisted class $\mathcal{S}$ constructions based on ADE Lie algebras of rank up to seven, as well as $A_8$ and $E_8$. We consider surfaces of genus at most three with up to five punctures, covering 167,244,647 constructions in total. To find candidate pairs of isomorphic theories, we compare Schur and Hall-Littlewood indices, Weyl anomalies, Coulomb branch spectra, and flavor data. We set aside pairs explained by known mechanisms, leaving a catalogue of 5,278 candidate pairs. Recurring changes in rank, puncture labels, and twists suggest families of candidate isomorphisms. We group 99.58% of the pairs into 25 families and 6 finite families. IndexLab is available at superconformal.com.

title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
abstract: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.

title: Hidden wormholes from an action principle in $D=4$
abstract: We present new black hole solutions for the class of gravitational effective field theories in four spacetime dimensions that extend General Relativity while retaining the graviton as the only degree of freedom of gravitational origin. We consider terms up to cubic order in curvature, solve the resulting field equations, and find one-way hidden wormholes as numerical solutions: these are regular black holes with an interior wormhole throat that is crossable in one direction and leads to a cosmological spacetime in its interior. They are regular and have no inner horizon, thus evading the mass inflation instability that afflicts conventional regular black hole geometries.

title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
abstract: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.

title: The Shape of the Strongly Coupled MQM Ground State
abstract: We study a surprisingly efficient family of variational ansatze for the ground state of bosonic matrix quantum mechanics at large $N$. These are ansatze whose norm-squared probability distributions are themselves matrix integrals with single-trace actions, and so have their own independent `t Hooft expansions. They are efficient in the sense that optimizing over a small number of parameters produces many digits of accuracy for the energy, single-trace moments, and connected correlators. For infinite-$N$ planar data our results rapidly converge to within published bootstrap intervals and stabilize to a few digits of precision beyond them. We also demonstrate that we can efficiently capture $1/N$ corrections by computing connected two-point functions. These are matched against resummed quantum perturbation theory and Monte Carlo simulations.

title: A separation criterion for chiral systems and its application to Plebański--Demiański perturbations
abstract: We give a constructive criterion for local separation of first-order chiral systems coupling two complex doublets. It combines a Gram decomposition of the coupling sources with separate coordinate dependence and a differential transport test. For recoverable, nondegenerate source families, the criterion is necessary and sufficient within the specified class of mode-independent complex matrix transformations with unit determinant. For a fixed differential operator and admissible Gram decomposition, we identify conditions under which the sources uniquely determine the Hermitian coefficient matrix required for separation. As an application, we construct an explicit algebraic transformation and derive separated radial and angular equations for coupled radiative Einstein--Maxwell perturbations of rotating, charged Plebański--Demiański backgrounds with acceleration, NUT charge, and a cosmological constant, on specified local patches. Its Gram decomposition is unique under additional generic assumptions. We also derive angular endpoint indices for Bonnor and Misner identifications with conical deficits or excesses. Under the stated regularity assumptions, each specified self-adjoint angular realization at fixed real mode parameters has a discrete spectrum and a complete orthonormal eigenbasis.

title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
abstract: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity. The resulting equations naturally decompose into contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher order paths through the network. We leverage this decomposition to express the effective monosynaptic connection between two neurons in terms of experimentally measurable statistics of the activity, and in particular, their high-frequency correlations. In this way, we show that it is possible to recover network connectivity from neural activity.

title: Exceptional cubics on 7-manifolds
abstract: A $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ on a $7$-manifold $\mathcal M$ determines a two-dimensional space of invariant totally symmetric cubic forms on each fiber of the rank-$27$ bundle $S^2_0T^*\mathcal M$ of traceless symmetric $2$-tensors. This space is spanned by the trace cubic $C_0$ and a cubic $C_\varphi$ that, up to a constant factor, is the pointwise integrand of the Yukawa coupling on the $G_2$ moduli space. We determine the exact infinitesimal stabilizers over $\mathbb C$ of all nonzero cubics in this family. For $C_0+λC_\varphi$, the stabilizer has dimension $78$ precisely at the two non-real values $λ_\pm=(1\pm i\sqrt7)/8$. Its dimension is $21$ for $C_0$ and $14$ in all other cases. At $λ_\pm$, the stabilizer is simple of type $E_6$, and the corresponding cubic is linearly equivalent to the complex Albert algebra cubic norm. The two cubics at $λ_\pm$, which we call critical, define complex-conjugate $E_6$-reductions of the complexified bundle. At any element with nonzero critical norm, the corresponding cubic determines a complex Albert algebra with basepoint stabilizer $F_4$; a line subbundle of the tangent bundle selects a smooth bundle of these algebras with tensorial operations and a Euclidean real form. The induced Levi-Civita connection preserves either critical cubic exactly when the $G_2$-structure is torsion-free. Its orthogonal projections onto the two exceptional reductions coincide with the connection induced by the minimal $G_2$-connection.
