New transformation relationships between these orbitals and Slater-type orbitals with noninteger principal quantum numbers are established. The radial differential equation is expressed in terms of the radial momentum operator. The expectation values of the position and radial momentum operators are obtained in closed form. The radial and Heisenberg uncertainty products, the Shannon entropy and the Fisher information are derived in general form.

title: The Spectral Anatomy of Complex-Time Singularities
abstract: The properties of the bulk spacetime in a holographic theory may be probed by the analytic structure of the boundary correlator $G(t,x)$. In this letter, we analyse the singularities of $G(t,x)$ by deriving them from Fourier space. We show that the quasinormal modes are characterised by two distinct momentum scaling regimes. The first regime is defined by a finite $k/ω^γ$ for some characteristic exponent $γ$ which is extracted from the singularity, and probes $G(t,0)$, reproducing the bouncing geodesic analysis. The second regime is defined by a finite $k/ω$, and probes the complexified bulk away from the singularity, which allows us to study the singularities of $G(t,x\neq 0)$. We extract coefficients and exponents of the singularities for general spacetime dimensions, and allow for more exotic interiors. The heavy reliance of our computation on quasinormal modes opens the doors to a similar analysis being done on spacetimes that are accessible only numerically.

title: Observables and Symmetries in Causal Fermion System
abstract: We investigate the interplay of observables and symmetries in the framework of causal fermion systems (CFS). We show that position observables transform covariantly under unitary symmetries and for static CFS we derive their Heisenberg-type evolution. To give these results a geometric interpretation, we establish conditions under which spacetime isometries induce symmetries of CFS constructed from solutions of the Dirac equation. The crucial link is provided by the Dirac equation itself, which relates the infinitesimal generators of the geometric and CFS symmetries. In static spacetimes, this allows us to identify the generator of the induced unitary symmetry with the spatial Dirac Hamiltonian.

title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
abstract: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process
abstract: Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph. We establish the exact conditions for attaining equality in the moving particle lemma for the interchange process on $G$ subject to a unit voltage drop across two terminal vertices $x\neq y \in V$. First, equality can occur only in irreducible representations indexed by partitions with at most two rows. We then show that the equality phenomenon beyond the constant and linear sectors is already visible in the two-particle exclusion process. Such equality occurs in exactly two cases: either the harmonic $x$--$y$ voltage is $\frac12$ on every nonterminal vertex, and the induced nonterminal graph $G[V\setminus\{x,y\}]$ is disconnected; or the harmonic voltage is constant on each connected component of $G[V\setminus \{x,y\}]$, and both voltage values $a$ and $1-a$, with $0\le a<\frac12$, occur. In each case we compute the equality kernel in every degree and particle sector. The resulting decomposition gives the complete equality kernel for exclusion and, through the regular representation, for the interchange process.

title: Exploring M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$: Mellin amplitudes with composite operators
abstract: We bootstrap mixed correlators in M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$, focusing on tree-level correlation functions involving one double-particle operator and three single-particle operators. Combining inputs from AdS/CFT, the chiral algebra, and the OPE at large central charge, we uniquely determine the Mellin amplitude for $\langle [{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{q}]{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{p}{\cal O}_{p+q-2}\rangle$ for generic $p$ and $q$. While our main focus is the $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT in six dimensions, we also derive the analogous result in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, applying the same bootstrap approach to $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. Despite their different dynamics, the resulting Mellin amplitudes exhibit a strikingly similar structure, with non-trivial OPE predictions for low-twist protected operators providing a key input. Our work is motivated by recent developments in the study of Kaluza-Klein correlators in bubbling geometries, where four-point functions involving single- and multi-particle operators are computed as response functions to smooth deformations of the vacuum geometry. While well tested in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, we aim to extend this framework to M-theory.

title: Maxwell's equations with thin wires in critical scaling
abstract: We derive effective equations for a situation in which electromagnetic waves hit an array of very thin wires. We study two cases, perfectly conducting wires and highly conducting wires, and investigate in both the critical scaling of the parameters. The electric field $E^η$ and the magnetic field $H^η$ satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations, and the small parameter $η>0$ is the spacing of the wires. A non-critical scaling of the wires implies either that the wires have no effect or that the tangential component of the limiting electric field in the direction of the wires vanishes along the effective interface. In the critical scaling, we observe an interesting effect: The wires act as oscillators and there is a relation between the electric field in longitudinal direction and the jump of the magnetic field in transversal direction involving second derivatives of a flux quantity.

title: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
abstract: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. In particular, this leads us to consider not only perturbations of the support, but also perturbations of the atoms' masses. On the other hand, using elementary techniques of Fourier analysis, we prove that any translation-bounded crystalline measure has a diffraction measure, and we explicitly compute its diffraction.

title: Gravitational Corrections to OPE Coefficients
abstract: The short-distance singular behavior of correlation functions of quantum field theories in curved spacetime is a universal property shared by all well-behaved states (known as Hadamard states). For two-point functions this takes the form of the Hadamard tail of free scalars and its generalizations to spinning fields and interacting theories. In this work, we compute similar universal curvature corrections to curved-space OPE coefficients in a short-distance expansion for interacting quantum field theories in general dimensions. We work at leading order in the curvature but for arbitrary backgrounds. Examples include weakly coupled scalar field theories with cubic and quartic interactions as well as strongly coupled conformal field theories. The gravitationally dressed OPE coefficients allow us to test explicitly, and confirm, the validity of the smearing-in-time procedure discussed by Witten in the construction of the algebra of observables near an observer's worldline in curved spacetime.

title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
abstract: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$. At $t=m=0$, the boundary contribution is power infrared divergent in four dimensions. Analytic continuation in DR conceals this divergence, which gives no $1/ε$ pole about $d=4$. At the critical dimension $d=6$, the same endpoint diverges logarithmically and gives a pole in the continued integral. Nonzero $t$ and finite $m$ regulate the same boundary region, yielding the known anomaly-related $1/t$ pole and a previously unreported $1/m^2$ behavior, respectively. We also show that a transverse gluon-polarization projector can eliminate an anomaly-related contribution that survives with explicit gluon polarization vectors. Finally, we present complete one-loop results for polarized and unpolarized DDVCS with all three infrared prescriptions. After summing the diagrams, the same evolution kernel governs the infrared pole in DR and the logarithms $\ln(Q^2/(-t))$ and $\ln(Q^2/m^2)$ within each polarization channel. This work establishes the common geometric origin of these anomaly-related poles within one-loop box amplitudes.

title: Exact ultrastatic multi-throat wormholes: Geometry, energy conditions, and optical cavities
abstract: We construct an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric, wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity. A factorized prescription for the derivative of the areal radius places every stationary sphere at a prescribed proper distance while retaining elementary integrability and asymptotic flatness. The order-$N$ geometry contains exactly $N+1$ throats and $N$ anti-throats, arranged as an alternating chain of necks and finite interior cavities. Independently of this particular hierarchy, the Einstein equations imply three universal ultrastatic results. Every nondegenerate throat violates the radial null energy condition, whereas every nondegenerate anti-throat satisfies the null, weak, dominant, and strong energy conditions, with the strong-energy sum condition saturated. The same local combination $ρ+p_\ell$ fixes the radial stability of the associated circular null orbit through $V_{\mathrm {null}}''=8πL^2(ρ+p_\ell)/\mathcal R^2$; throats are therefore unstable light rings and anti-throats are stable ones. Finally, every finite cell between consecutive stationary spheres, each exterior cell, and the complete two-ended radial null geodesic carry strictly negative integrated radial null energy. The resulting spacetimes are exact multi-cavity optical chains whose cavity centers are locally nonexotic even though no cell can eliminate averaged radial exoticity. The first nontrivial member interpolates continuously from the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a quartically degenerate throat to a double-throat geometry and admits closed expressions for its source, null average, branchwise Morris-Thorne form, embedding criterion, and traversability scales. Its vanishing Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass follows from the specific radial falloff of the hierarchy, rather than from ultrastaticity alone.

title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
abstract: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.

title: Potential Flow, Stress, and Straightness in Flow Matching: Euler Error on Gaussian-Mixture Targets
abstract: In linear flow matching, coupling straightness measures conditional displacement variance. The conditional covariance gives a kinetic stress in the Jeans balance. The virial identity relates the mean trace of the covariance to a radial moment of acceleration. Euler error also depends on how the flow propagates acceleration. On constructed Gaussian-mixture targets, closed-form couplings with matched straightness yield different median Euler errors. Learned fields from fresh minibatch assignments also yield different Euler errors from their partners at matched estimated straightness. The leading Euler coefficient accounts for more of the error variation than straightness in these experiments. We relate the additive-noise characterization of isotropic Gaussian sources to potential flow. A gradient constraint reduces velocity error on the independent isotropic Gaussian example and increases it on two examples with rotational exact fields.

title: Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation
abstract: In this paper Bäcklund transformations of the fifth Painlevé equation are discussed. The Bäcklund transformations are applied to rational solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation, which are expressed in terms of the generalised Laguerre polynomials and generalised Umemura polynomials. Using appropriate Bäcklund transformations, we derive non-unique solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation in terms of modified Bessel functions. Further it is shown that there are also rational solutions in terms of generalised Umemura polynomials for the same values of the parameters, which are not special cases of the modified Bessel function solutions. The relationship between solutions of the fifth Painlevé equation and solutions of the third Painlevé equation is also discussed.

title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
abstract: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=λΔ+\tanπ(θ+n^2α)δ_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $λ>0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(α, θ)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tanπ(θ+n^2α)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $α\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.

title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
abstract: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

title: Towards an improved understanding of $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors
abstract: The isovector axial-vector and tensor meson states $a_1$ and $a_2$ have garnered interest in the last years since they appear as intermediate states in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution to $(g-2)_μ$. Their dynamical behaviour including their transition form factors is poorly understood to this day, which also affects the uncertainty budget of the HLbL contribution. In order to improve the situation, we construct the $a_1$ and $a_2$ as resonances in the $ρπ$ system, which allows us to express the relevant amplitudes in terms of known form factors and properties of the resonances. With this, we aim to obtain a phenomenologically well motivated parameterisation of the transition form factors built from the general principles of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry.

title: On the dynamics of N classical particles interacting with a complex environment
abstract: The interactions of a particle with its environment eventually lead to the damping of its motion. This phenomenom is well understood when considering a single particle exchanging energy with the environment. The situation is definitely more complex when many particles are considered: the energy dissipation mechanisms are not clear whenever particles create a common well in which they keep interacting. In this framework, we identify the equilibrium solutions, that consist in clusters of particles at rest, and we establish their spectral stability. We show that the mean position/velocity pair is damped exponentially fast at the linearized level. Coming back to the non linear problem, we can show, at least in some simplified cases, that the dissipation mechanisms also involve far slower rates, that explain the difficulty in observing the relaxation behavior on the individual trajectories.

title: Inverse energy transfer for 2D Navier--Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse
abstract: We prove inverse energy transfer for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse, confirming the 1979 prediction of Novikov and Sedov. Nonlinear interactions transfer kinetic energy from high to low frequencies over a common time interval that shrinks to the collapse time as the viscosity tends to zero. We prove that the net nonlinear transfer over this interval converges to the same positive constant across an expanding range of frequency cutoffs, with quantitative error bounds uniform in the cutoff.

title: Fer expansion converges almost twice as far as Magnus for qubits
abstract: The Fer expansion writes the propagator of a time-dependent Hamiltonian as a product of unitary exponentials whose error decreases doubly exponentially with the number of factors, while the Magnus expansion improves by one order at a time. Its convergence, however, was guaranteed only below a radius of about $2.6058$, smaller than the Magnus radius $π$. We establish a guaranteed convergence threshold of about $6.2106$, or $1.98\,π$, for a qubit. This is almost twice the optimal universal Magnus threshold $π$; the bound on a single Fer step is sharp, while the exact convergence radius remains open.

title: Generalised $Ω$-backgrounds in twisted $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills
abstract: We introduce rigid supergravity backgrounds for 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills which deform its topological twists and generalise the $Ω$-deformation of $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theories. We derive the twisted supersymmetry variations of the $\mathcal{N}=4$ Weyl multiplet, and the $\mathcal{N}=4$ matter multiplet coupled to a rigid bosonic background, for each of the three inequivalent topological twists. Other, more exotic backgrounds are also discussed.

title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
abstract: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

title: Destabilization of Abelian-Higgs vortices at large Chern-Simons coupling
abstract: We study the effect of the Chern--Simons (CS) coupling on the radial spectral stability of axially symmetric vortices in the $(2+1)$-dimensional Abelian--Higgs model. From the linear stability approach, we obtain the dispersion relations of gauge field perturbations, which signal the existence of a critical CS coupling $k_{\rm c}$ that depends on Maxwell's coupling constant. For $k<k_{\rm c}$, the continuous spectrum is purely imaginary and the modes remain gapped. At $k=k_{\rm c}$, one of the modes becomes gapless, while for $k>k_{\rm c}$ real eigenvalues appear, corresponding to exponentially growing radial modes. Direct time-evolution simulations are consistent with the spectral analysis, which shows instability for $k>k_{\rm c}$. Below the threshold, the perturbed vortex relaxes toward its stationary profile, whereas above the threshold, growing fluctuations deform the core and propagate outward. These results show that the CS coupling controls radial spectral stability of Abelian-Higgs vortices, and destabilization occurs for sufficiently large CS coupling, relative to the Maxwell coupling.

title: Painlevé quadrics and their confluence for the dispersionless Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
abstract: We construct and study a distinguished class of solutions of the dispersionless Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (dKP) equation whose geometry is governed by the first and second Painlevé equations. The level surfaces of these solutions correspond to three geometric families of central quadrics, and we determine when their level surfaces degenerate into planes. In the parabolic family parametrised by $\mathrm{P_I}$, degenerate levels occur at the stationary points of the transcendent. For the hyperbolic family parametrised by rational solutions of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$, we show that degenerate levels occur at points where consecutive solutions intersect and we give a precise count of such degeneracies. In the homogeneous elliptic family, the Hastings--McLeod solution of $\mathrm{P_{II}}$ is characterised, up to sign, as the unique non-trivial real pole-free solution with Airy asymptotics whose quadric has no finite degenerate level. Finally, under critical scaling, the quadrics generated by the $n$-th rational Painlevé-II solution converge locally, and away from poles, to the parabolic quadrics associated with the Painlevé-I tritronquée solution, with error $O(n^{-1/5})$.

title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
abstract: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

title: Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
abstract: The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.

title: The Thermodynamic Limit and the Landau degeneracy
abstract: Usually, thermodynamic quantities are calculated by first regularizing the system in a confining box, which may have hard walls or periodic boundaries. One then studies the finite system and takes the thermodynamic limit by letting the box grow indefinitely. Here, we discuss a regularization scheme devised in the late 1980s [1] to study the thermodynamic equations of an anyon gas [2]. Instead of confining the system with walls, the method adds a smooth harmonic potential. Quantities are evaluated in its presence, and the potential is then gradually removed. A suitable prescription for taking this limit is needed to obtain meaningful thermodynamic results.

title: Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and $Z$ boson anomalous couplings
abstract: The Higgs boson self-coupling enters the Higgsstrahlung process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at one loop. The three diagrams that carry it project onto two Lorentz structures: the tree-level one, which rescales the rate, and that of the CP-even anomalous coupling $b_Z$, which changes the polarization of the final-state $Z$ boson. To assess how well quantum state tomography constrains the $hZZ$ anomalous couplings and the trilinear coupling at FCC-ee, we compute the helicity density matrix of the $Z$ boson, for an effective vertex that also includes a CP-odd anomalous coupling $\tilde b_Z$, together with its complete one-loop correction in the Standard Model. With these corrections and no other new physics in the effective vertex, quantum state tomography determines $κ_λ$ to $\pm 3.9$, or $\pm 2.9$ with the full angular information, independently of the rate and of the normalization of the vertex, and not far from the limit $δκ_λ\simeq 1$ set by the quantum Fisher information. Without assumptions on the new physics, quantum tomography directly bounds the anomalous couplings at the $10^{-3}$ level, improving on the existing projections. The density matrix also characterizes the $Z$ boson as a qutrit. At $365$ GeV its state in the central region is pure enough to violate the Klyachko--Can--Binicioğlu--Shumovsky contextuality inequality, $\mathbb{CNTXT}_5 = 2.06$ at $θ= π/2$ against the non-contextual bound $2$. We also quantify the purity and the amount of magic of the $Z$ boson state, using the mana, the stabilizer Rényi entropy and the robustness of magic for the latter. At fixed angle, purity, contextuality and magic are robust against anomalous couplings of the size probed by the tomography. The inclusive state, instead, is neither contextual in this test nor magic in the helicity basis.

title: Quantum Preparation without Disturbance: Information Costs and Hypothesis Testing
abstract: We determine the minimum information cost of preparing either of two quantum states with one common device while preserving its memory. Measured by the Umegaki relative entropy between the two possible memory states, this minimum is the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy of the target states. If the memory may instead be consumed, the minimum is their Umegaki relative entropy. More generally, for any divergence satisfying data processing, memory preservation selects the maximal extension of its classical restriction. We also study the cost of requiring only finitely many outputs, with the costs increasing from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy as the number of outputs grows. Finally, we consider hypothesis testing of an unknown device over independent runs. The optimal Stein exponent per run converges to the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy whenever the number of outputs per run diverges. This gives an operational characterization of the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy in quantum statistics.

title: Mirror symmetry of $\mathcal{N}=(0,4)$ boundary conditions with Nahm poles
abstract: We propose mirror symmetry between $\mathcal{N}=(0,4)$ boundary conditions with Nahm poles and Neumann boundary conditions with boundary Fermi multiplets in 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ non-Abelian gauge theories, including $U(N)$ SQCD, $T[SU(N)]$ and the ADHM theories. We obtain the half-indices of the Nahm pole boundary conditions from those of the Dirichlet boundary conditions by Higgsing, where the boundary fugacities are specialized along the principal embedding of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. We check that they agree with the half-indices of the dual Neumann boundary conditions. In the twist limits they give closed-form formulas for the vacuum characters of the boundary vertex operator algebras of Costello and Gaiotto. We find that the unflavored vacuum characters are eta-quotients times quasimodular forms, which we write explicitly in terms of Eisenstein series for all our examples.

title: Modular Structure of the ADHM Effective Twisted Superpotential
abstract: The Cardy limit of M2-brane indices retains nonperturbative information through the effective twisted superpotential, including corrections exponentially suppressed at large rank. We investigate the flavor dependence of these corrections in the three-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ $\mathrm U(N)$ ADHM theory at the universal twist. For $N_f=1,2,4$ fundamental hypermultiplets, we conjecture that the full exponential remainder of the selected Bethe critical value is an absolutely convergent divisor sum obtained by applying a first-order differential operator to an Eichler integral of a weight-four Eisenstein form. Resolving this remainder requires the additive constant, which we evaluate from its known integral representation as finite Clausen sums for every positive integer $N_f$. Expanding the integral together with the shifted-rank power determines the type-IIA coefficients of the perturbative contribution at arbitrary genus and their factorial growth. With this subtraction fixed, the proposed sums reproduce independently computed Bethe critical values at up to $800$-digit accuracy, including low ranks that test the continuation beyond the reconstructed sectors. The flavor-one expression agrees with level-one ABJM, whereas the two- and four-flavor completions have distinct divisor laws related by exact dissection identities to finite combinations of ABJM functions. The comparison supports a shared weight-four organization of nonperturbative Bethe data beyond the mirror pair, with arithmetic that distinguishes the theories. Through the finite-rank Cardy relation, the proposed completion predicts the entire $1/ω$ coefficient of the selected vacuum contribution to the superconformal index, retaining these theory-dependent corrections in its leading exponent.

title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlevé Equation
abstract: For the first Painlevé equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_π\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-π}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8π/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2π/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlevé transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.

title: Evidence for the decay $B^0 \to μ^+ μ^-$ and improved measurements of the decay $B^0_s \to μ^+ μ^-$
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
abstract: The first single-experiment evidence for the rare decay $B^0 \to μ^+ μ^-$ and the world's most precise measurements of the $B^0_s \to μ^+ μ^-$ branching fraction and effective lifetime are reported. The results are obtained using Run 3 proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 18 fb$^{-1}$ recorded with the LHCb Upgrade I detector at a centre-of-mass energy of $13.6$ TeV between 2024 and 2025. Their combination with the Run 1 and Run 2 LHCb results further improves the precision. All measurements are found to be in agreement with the Standard Model expectations.

title: Spectrum of a 2D QFT analogue of the SYK model
abstract: We study the spectrum of the two-dimensional generalisation of the SYK model proposed by Turiaci and Verlinde, in which chiral Majorana fermions with a topological kinetic term interact through random $2q$-fermion couplings. We compute the four-point function at order $1/N$ in the conformal limit. In addition to the conformal Casimir, the ladder kernels commute with the operator that exchanges a single lightcone coordinate. As a result, the four-point function splits into an even and an odd sector, which the kernels do not mix. In each sector we construct a complete eigenbasis of the Casimir, find the eigenvalues of the kernels in closed form and sum the ladder diagrams. The poles in the ladder sum lie on a spectral curve in the plane of the two conformal weights. A conformal solution in the IR limit breaks the symmetries of the model under chiral reparametrisations and local Lorentz transformations, and the kernel has eigenvalue one on the corresponding modes. The reparametrisation modes, with conformal weights $(2,0)$ and $(0,2)$, are non-normalisable, whereas the Lorentz mode of the odd sector, with weights $(1,1)$, is normalisable. We determine the region where the sum of ladders can be represented in a contour form analogous to that of the one-dimensional SYK model.

title: Hidden Quantum Markov Processes: Mealy Formulation and Observable Reduction
abstract: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with a boundary state, it generates a quasi-local, finitely correlated hidden--output state; for the commutative generator associated with a classical Mealy kernel, this state is the full joint law of the classical Mealy model. Moore realizations correspond to transition expectations that factor on the prescribed hidden algebra. We establish a rank obstruction to such factorization and prove its sufficiency for isometric generators: factorization holds exactly when the induced hidden-memory channel has Kraus rank at most the hidden Hilbert-space dimension. The Kraus rank also gives the minimal intermediate Hilbert-space dimension. When the hidden and output dimensions are at least two, the factorizable isometric generators form a closed subset of measure zero. For any fixed projective readout, a Mealy generator induces an operational hidden quantum Markov model in the sense of Monràs, Beige and Wiesner; conversely, every finite-dimensional operational model admits a Mealy lift on the same memory space with a rank-one readout. For their cluster-state instrument, two isometric, Moore-factorizable lifts with the same instrument and initial memory state yield identical measured output statistics but different quantum output states: one has marginals entangled across $1|2\cdots n$ for $n\geq3$, with three-output negativity $\tfrac12$, whereas the other has fully separable marginals. Thus operational equivalence does not determine output entanglement.

title: Second order and secondary functional renormalization group flow equations
abstract: The functional renormalization group provides a powerful non-perturbative framework for quantum field theory through the exact flow equation for the scale-dependent effective action. A mass-type regulator $R_k = k^2$ is particularly attractive because it preserves symmetries, locality, and unitarity (or Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity in the Euclidean domain). However, unlike momentum-dependent regulators, it does not tame all ultraviolet divergences: in four dimensions, flow equations for the effective potential exhibit logarithmic divergences. Motivated by Callan's perturbative renormalization scheme, where higher-order $θ$-insertions improve ultraviolet convergence, we develop two classes of higher-order functional flow equations. First, we derive exact second-order flow equations by taking further derivatives of the standard flow equation with respect to $k$. These have either a one-loop structure involving the first derivative of the inverse propagator, or a mixed one-loop and two-loop structure. While exact and useful for incorporating two-loop effects and testing truncation schemes, they do not in general resolve the ultraviolet convergence problem. Second, we introduce a secondary flow method, where variations of an effective mass-squared parameter introduce an additional flow, with parameter $l$. The resulting secondary flow equations become ultraviolet finite once sufficiently many derivatives have been taken, and can be evaluated without an additional ultraviolet regulator. Integrating back to the standard flow requires integration constants that encode microscopic ultraviolet physics, analogous to relevant coupling constants.

title: Metastable vortex string decay in a brane picture
abstract: We describe the decay of a metastable string as a bounce in a brane configuration. We consider a particular $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric $\mathrm{U}(2)$ gauge theory with cascade Higgsing $\mathrm{U}(2)\to \mathrm{U}(1)^2 \to \mathrm{U}(1)$, where the vortex string can break by creating a pair of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopole and anti-monopole. The theory is engineered in a Type IIA brane setup, where the metastable string is realized as a D2-brane stretched between NS5- and D4-branes. The string breaks when the endpoints of the D2-brane, moving along the NS5- and D4-branes, meet so that the D2-brane shrinks to nothing. We check that the tension of the D2-brane reproduces that of the vortex string obtained numerically in the field theory, with the ratio approaching one in the limit where the vortex string becomes BPS. Within the thin-wall approximation, we derive the bounce action from the Dirac-Born-Infeld action of the D2-brane and find that it agrees with that of the field theory, with the monopole mass given by the area swept by the D2-brane. As a consistency check, we numerically construct a bounce solution of the D2-brane equation of motion under simplifying assumptions, whose action agrees with the thin-wall result in the regime where our description is reliable.

title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
abstract: We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity $q$ and Fermi momentum $k=(6π^2ρ/q)^{1/3}$, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy \[ D_{\rm M}(k)=\frac{3}{4π^2}\log k+O(1),\qquad D_{\rm CHF}(k)=12e^{-1/2-π^2/8} k^2e^{-π^{3/2}\sqrt{k}}(1+o(1)). \] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted $L^2$ convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

title: ADfiRe: An empirical- and CFD-informed advection-diffusion-reaction thermal model for wildfire spread
abstract: Real-time wildfire forecasting requires a trade-off between rapid yet physically relevant models and high fidelity but computationally costly models of flame spread over heterogeneous, multiphase solid fuel. The present study introduces ADfiRe, a hybrid framework that integrates empirical correlations and CFD-informed parameterizations into a physics-based advection-diffusion-reaction (ADR) formulation. The key features of ADfiRe are the use of established fuel databases, the capacity to handle multiple fuels, and a methodology to capture the effect of arbitrary topography. Furthermore, it includes the effect of flame tilting due to wind, thus accounting for the differences between plume- and wind-dominated fire propagation. ADfiRe resolves explicitly the coupled thermochemical degradation as well as heat and mass transport mechanisms of the advancing fire front. The wind field is modeled based on an appropriately defined Byram number. The model is validated against five well-documented experimental field-scale fires in Mediterranean shrublands, showing quantitative agreement with key metrics such as the rate of spread (ROS) and the fireline intensity, through a two-stage, Arrhenius-based heterogeneous reaction scheme coupling solid-fuel pyrolysis and oxygen-limited char/volatile combustion.

title: The cone of states over time: exact tests and convergent two-sided hierarchies
abstract: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $ρ$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(ρ\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. We study the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ generated by these operators. Our main result is a convergent outer semidefinite hierarchy with an explicit trace-norm Hausdorff bound on its trace-one slices. Specializing constrained symmetric-extension theory to the input--channel representation, we show that Bose-extension rounding preserves the channel marginal constraint and gives error at most $2d_A^2(d_A-1)/(k+d_A-1)$ at level $k$. A complementary inner hierarchy retains all channels at each chosen pure-input direction. For $d_A\ge2$, its error is at most $2(d_A-1)\sin^2δ$, where $δ$ is the Fubini--Study covering radius; nested sets of $N$ directions give error at most $2π^2(d_A-1)N^{-1/(d_A-1)}$, independently of $d_B$. These bounds provide explicit size--accuracy guarantees and certified support-value bounds, without guaranteeing finite termination for exact boundary membership. For binary classical outputs, we obtain an exact SDP membership test, including indefinite output blocks and mixtures that are not single stotes. At faithful marginal the test reduces to a scalar inequality; every trace-one member of this sector with input marginal $ρ$ has a constructive realization using at most $\operatorname{rank}ρ$ pure-input stotes with binary measurement channels. Finally, we compute the exact isotropic boundary and prove $\mathrm{PPT}\subsetneq\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}\cap\mathrm{PSD}\subsetneq\mathrm{PSD}$ for equal local dimensions at least two.

title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
abstract: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $δ$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.

title: BeST: Beta splatted tomography for direct reconstruction from coherent imaging measurements
abstract: Conventional coherent X-ray tomography requires the phase of each projection to be reconstructed with high fidelity. However, individual reconstructed projections might be flawed, e.g. due to positioning errors, yielding inconsistent tomographic reconstructions. By directly coupling phase retrieval and tomography, consistency is enforced through a common object volume. But reconstructing a full volume demands substantial computational resources. To reduce this demand, we introduce Beta Splatted Tomography (BeST), which represents the common object volume using compactly supported beta primitives with closed-form analytical projections, enabling efficient reconstruction directly from coherent scattering images. This representation substantially reduces the number of optimizable parameters compared to a voxel grid. We demonstrate BeST on experimental datasets from hard X-ray near-field holography and far-field ptychography measurements. In both cases, the joint technique improves reconstruction quality compared to two-step methods.

title: General $δN$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $δN$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.

title: Gravitational form factors of $ρ$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD
abstract: We compute the gravitational form factors and mechanical properties of the $ρ$ and $a_1$ mesons in V-QCD, a holographic model of QCD with backreacting flavor and dynamical chiral symmetry breaking. The parameters of the model are taken from an earlier fit to meson spectra and are not adjusted to form factor data. Both mesons are described by a single spin-1 field, and the six form factors are identified from the matrix element of the energy-momentum tensor with two spin-1 states, following the holographic dictionary. We find that $A_0 = J$ and $A_1 = 0$ hold identically in the model, and show that the remaining form factors $E$, $D_0$ and $D_1$ are regular at zero momentum transfer. We compare the form factors of $ρ$ with results from the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, a light-cone constituent quark model and the hard-wall holographic model. From the form factors, we compute the monopole and quadrupole distributions of energy, pressure and shear force in the Breit frame. The D-term, defined for spin-1 hadrons as the forward value of the combination $\mathcal{D}_0(t)$ of form factors, is found to be $-2.98$ for the $ρ$ and $-7.43$ for the $a_1$ meson. The mass and mechanical radii are $0.81$~fm and $0.89$~fm for $ρ$, and $0.73$~fm and $0.80$~fm for $a_1$.

title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform-mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2σ$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.

title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

title: Projection of massive and interacting conformal theories to the future null infinity
abstract: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a Møller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.

title: Complexity and symmetry: The asymmetry factor approach
abstract: We study the influence of the instantaneous appearance of a time-like Killing vector (TKV) in self-gravitating fluid spheres during their evolution. For doing so we resort to the concept of asymmetry factor which allows the existence of any specific type of symmetry (e.g. a TKV), exclusively, for a given value of the time-like coordinate. We consider adiabatic and dissipative fluids. The analysis of different relevant physical variables in this process shows the imprints of the emergence of TKV at some point of the evolution. Particular attention is paid to the relationship appearing between the TKV, and the complexity factor describing the degree of complexity of the fluid, bringing out for the first time a link between complexity and symmetry.

title: Carrollian minimal massive gravity and the fate of third-way consistency
abstract: We construct the Carrollian limit of minimal massive gravity. The limit is singular for the algebra and regular for the Chern-Simons-like data. The one divergent bracket points along the null direction of the contracted bilinear form. The Lagrangian is therefore finite while the brackets are not. The contracted curvature still obeys a cubic closure condition, forced on shell rather than identically. The third-way coupling itself, however, is removable. For generic parameters an invertible redefinition of the auxiliary field and the boost connection takes it to Carrollian topologically massive gravity up to a boundary term. The same redefinition fails before the limit. We solve for an anti-de Sitter vacuum and a Carrollian black hole, whose rotation parameter leaves the frame and survives only in the boost connection. The degenerate vector flavor metric obstructs the standard charge formula, which we replace by a canonical one. The boundary charges, obtained in two independent ways, carry no trace of the deformation. A Dirac analysis gives nine first-class constraints and no local degrees of freedom on any background. The massive graviton is removed. The asymptotic symmetry algebra is bms_3, with central charges carried by the Einstein and Lorentz-Chern-Simons terms. The black hole has two sets of thermodynamic data, each with its own first law. One obeys the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, the other keeps the Chern-Simons entropy.

title: Classical weak antilocalization in electron hydrodynamics
abstract: Weak localization is strongly suppressed in electron hydrodynamics, where frequent electron--electron collisions rapidly dephase the Cooperon. Nevertheless, disorder can still produce a logarithmic correction to the bare hydrodynamic resistivity. We show that spatial fluctuations of the momentum-relaxation rate generate a classical memory kernel through the diffusive return of transverse momentum. In two dimensions, this return is logarithmic, as in weak localization, but involves a single shear propagator rather than quantum interference. Conservation laws and positivity of dissipation fix its antilocalizing sign: the return reduces momentum relaxation and hence the bulk resistivity. Unlike quantum weak localization, the logarithm is cut off by momentum relaxation and has a viscosity-dependent amplitude. For temperature-independent impurity friction, the resistivity correction scales as $-T^2\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Fermi liquid and $-T\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Planckian metal. In channels, the return competes with viscosity renormalization, and a width scan separates the two effects.

title: The speed of convergence for propagation of chaos in the mean-field Ising model
abstract: We derive sharp relative-entropy asymptotics for increasing propagation of chaos in the Curie--Weiss model at zero external field. For every fixed inverse temperature $0<β<1$, the relative entropy of a $k$-spin marginal with respect to the symmetric product measure is $$ \frac{β^2}{4(1-β)^2}\frac{k(k-1)}{N^2}+o\left(\frac{k^2}{N^2}\right),\qquad k=o(N). $$ At the critical inverse temperature $β=1$, the rate changes to $α_{\mathrm c}^2 k(k-1)/(4N)+o(k^2/N)$ in the regime $k=o(\sqrt N)$, where $α_{\mathrm c}$ is the second moment of the limiting quartic law of the rescaled magnetization. We also obtain asymptotics for sequences $β_N\uparrow1$ that interpolate between these two regimes. Crucially, the proof reveals that the pair correlations determine the leading correction to the likelihood ratio, providing precise control of both the chi-square divergence and relative entropy.

title: Sensitivity to $Θ^+$ production in the $π^- p \to K^- X$ reaction at HIAF-HIRIBL
abstract: Pion-induced searches for the $Θ^+$ can probe the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation region beyond the E19 energies. We present sensitivity projections for a missing-mass search for a narrow $Θ^+$ at 1.540 GeV/$c^2$ in $π^- p \to K^- X$ at the High Intensity heavy-ion Accelerator Facility and its HIgh-rigidity Radioactive Ion Beam Line. With the E19 resolutions, efficiency, and continuum, separate 10-day exposures at pion momenta of 2.01 and 2.586 GeV/$c$ give background-only median expected 90% CL upper limits of 0.0293 and 0.0356 $μ$b/sr, respectively, on the differential cross section averaged over $2^\circ$ to $15^\circ$ on the selected high-momentum branch; the higher momentum corresponds to the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation energy. Median local $5σ$ discovery thresholds are 0.0894 and 0.109 $μ$b/sr. Nonresonant nucleon-exchange models give width scales of 0.0039 to 0.079 MeV for $J^P=1/2^+$ and 0.045 to 1.47 MeV for $J^P=1/2^-$. All positive-parity variants would test the DIANA width scale of $0.34 \pm 0.10$ MeV; negative-parity sensitivity depends on the variant.

title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$μ$C: Nucleus Options
abstract: Nucleus options of the LH$μ$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $μ^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $μ$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $μ$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $μ$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $μ$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

title: Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)
abstract: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincaré algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.

title: Phases of deformed sine dilaton gravity and JT limit
abstract: We study the implications of marginal deformation in sine dilaton gravity (sDG). We investigate the thermodynamic properties of deformed sine dilaton gravity (dsDG) and examine the phase stability of black holes in two space-time dimensions. We found that the deformation parameter ($λ$) sets a critical temperature threshold ($T_0$). Below this critical value ($T<T_0$), the system enters an unphysical phase characterized by a fractional density of states and a negative Wald entropy. Above the critical temperature ($T>T_0$), we obtain a physical black hole phase with positive entropy and negative free energy. Furthermore, we evaluate the Komar integral, derive the Casimir function for dsDG, and establish the first law of black hole thermodynamics. Finally, we explore the infrared (IR) limit of dsDG which we identify as Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity accompanied by marginal deformation. We also perform a detailed analysis of various thermodynamic entities pertinent to this deformed JT solution.

title: Localization for Lipschitz monotone quasi-periodic operators with power-law hopping
abstract: We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on $\mathbb Z^d$ with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent $r$ exceeds the Diophantine exponent $τ$. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales. We use homotopy in the coupling constant to select the local eigenvalue branches and Schur complement estimates to control the successive elimination of coordinates.

title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data
abstract: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $θ_i=φ_i/f\in[0,π]$, conditioned on $π-θ_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2πf)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. The broad-prior model favors recent thawing, with median $w_{{\rm DE},0}=-0.865^{+0.068}_{-0.053}$, $m_φ\in[0.91,4.39]\times10^{-33}$ eV, and $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.589,4.899]$ (central 68\% credible intervals). Bayes factors relative to flat $Λ$CDM are 0.70 and 30.1 for the normalized fluctuation-conditioned prior (Convention I) and its further conditioning on numerical acceptance (Convention II). Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Relative to the zero-vacuum axion model, the broad-prior Bayes factors are 0.620 and 1.65, providing no compelling evidence for a negative cosmological constant. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $Λ$CDM. For this model, assuming that the instanton generating $m_φ^2f^2=Λ_{\rm UV}^4e^{-S_{\rm inst}}$ satisfies the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, the one-sided 95\% posterior lower limit on the minimum compatible coefficient $c_{\min}$ rises from 37 to 55 as the ultraviolet scale $Λ_{\rm UV}$ increases from $10^{-10}M_{\rm Pl}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$, in tension with an order-one coefficient under these assumptions.

title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

title: Cubic local observability of Gaussian-blind sources in thermal $φ^4_2$ fields
abstract: We study external sources that are invisible to a spatially local observation in a massive Gaussian thermal field on a circle. A quadratic-reference calibration removes the first-order thermal mass-shift signal. For the resulting quartic model we prove a cutoff-independent, source-uniform $C^1$ expansion of local Wick cubic means. Its leading operator has the time-integrated cube of the thermal covariance as its kernel. A positive bilateral Laplace representation proves injectivity on the entire external source space, while analyticity gives exponential singular-value upper bounds. The expansion yields local Araki relative-entropy lower bounds on every fixed finite-dimensional source space, and a uniform separation theorem at every prescribed Sobolev resolution. Under an additional interval-length condition, a reflection-positivity identity yields an explicit, nonoptimal double-logarithmic conditional stability bound for this specific thermal kernel. Continuum probability estimates and the integrability assumptions of the Feynman--Kac--Nelson construction are verified in Section~3.

title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
abstract: We determine the spaces of \(δ\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(δ\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(δ=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(δ=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

title: Dynamical Gauss--Bonnet Sum Rules and Global Consistency in Five-Dimensional Braneworld Cosmology
authors: Paulo Michel Longo Tavares da Silva
abstract: We derive an exact dynamical consistency relation for a smooth, periodically compactified five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet cosmology sourced by a real, minimally coupled canonical scalar field. For a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaitre--Robertson--Walker slicing and a generally time-dependent warp factor, a contraction of the bulk equations eliminates both the scalar potential and the bulk cosmological constant. A direct orthonormal-curvature reconstruction gives the independent diagonal and mixed field equations and verifies the contracted Gauss--Bonnet identity. The integrated relation separates an exact total derivative from the dynamically active Lovelock sector. Importantly, satisfying the integrated sum rule alone does not imply a solution of the complete system. We prove that, for positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling, a smooth periodic time-independent warp factor and a canonical scalar exclude all exact expanding power-law scale factors $a(t)\propto t^p$ with $p>0$. This strengthens the previously established de Sitter sign obstruction and removes an earlier interpretation of $p=1/2$ as an admissible sign-compatible physical branch. For time-dependent warping, we reformulate bouncing conditions using proper time and the physical scale factor on each constant-$y$ hypersurface. We compare the common $w=-1$ geometric member with the perturbative weighted construction of Dias, Hoff da Silva, and da Rocha. At the level of the unexpanded Ricci-trace rearrangement, the curvature-only tensor contribution differs from the full Lanczos contraction by a definite scalar-curvature term. This distinction, and the additional independent field equations, delimit the physical conclusions that may be drawn from a necessary integrated condition.

title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

title: Entanglement-to-Stress Relation from an Effective Holographic Description of the Transverse-Field Ising Model
abstract: We investigate an effective holographic description of the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM). We reconstruct the spatial metric from its entanglement entropy and determine the temporal metric using the Einstein-scalar equations, ultraviolet time normalization, and a smooth, horizonless center. Holographic renormalization then gives an enthalpy density that can be expressed through the entropy curvature at half the system size. This relation is a prediction of the effective gravity for the microscopic theory. We test it against the exact finite-size TFIM stress, which is not used in the reconstruction. Away from criticality, the gravity prediction agrees closely with the exact stress in the near-critical scaling regime. This result suggests an entanglement-to-stress relation in the massive Ising field theory, whose field-theoretic derivation remains open.
