Moore wrote the general solution for the field in terms of a function that satisfies a functional equation nowadays known as the Moore equation.In the literature, exact analytical solutions to the Moore equation form a rather small set, restricted to specific classes of laws of motion. Cole and Schieve (1995) developed a geometrical approach that yielded a general formula for the solution of the Moore equation for cavities initially at rest. However, its application has always been done through numerical calculations, and their approach has therefore long been regarded solely as a numerical method. In this work, we show that their method can also be employed as a powerful method for deriving exact analytical solutions, and show the applicability of this approach to deriving analytical solutions to the Moore equation. We obtain original exact analytical solutions for an expanding cavity with a uniformly moving mirror, a contracting cavity with a mirror that approaches the static one asymptotically, and, in addition, we recover the first analytical solution to the Moore equation for a resonant mirror motion, originally obtained by Law in 1994. Moreover, we extend the Cole-Schieve approach, showing that exact solutions can be constructed from any spacetime region where the Moore function has already been determined. We show that this extended geometrical approach allows us to expand the set of known analytical solutions to the Moore equation from the few classes of motion reported in the literature to an infinite set, as it enables the treatment of new classes of laws of motion obtained by combining those presented here with each other as well as with previously known classes of trajectories.

title: Liberation in the Heavy Limit
abstract: We study CFT four-point functions of identical scalar primaries as their dimension $Δ$ grows for fixed $0<z, \bar z<1$, and call them liberated if they grow at the same exponential rate as those of a generalized free field (GFF), as is the case for heavy free particles propagating along geodesics in AdS. We show that the correlator is liberated at the crossing symmetric point if and only if the light spectrum is sparse, and that liberation then holds wherever $z$ and $\bar z$ lie on the same side of $1/2$. If the low twist states are also sparse, liberation holds everywhere except in an explicit band around $z+\bar z=1$. In particular, if the primary twist gap lies above $\sqrt{2}Δ$, then the correlator is liberated everywhere. For twist cutoffs below $Δ$, composites of two spinning generalized free fields fail to be liberated in a region that fills the band near the double lightcone limit. In two dimensions, Virasoro primaries cannot be liberated unless the central charge grows faster than $Δ$. The same framework sharpens the universality of large-$c$ torus partition functions of two-dimensional CFTs.

title: HEART: a resonance-cascade model of soft hadron production in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c
abstract: Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 identified-hadron spectra in p+p collisions at 158 GeV/c as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This paper supplies an event-level realization of that picture, the HEART model (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), and tests it on the published NA49 data. Single diffraction, double diffraction, and non-diffractive exchange produce color-singlet excited systems. Each system is a catalogued resonance below a duality boundary of 1.7 to 2.2 GeV or a member of a resonant continuum above it. It de-excites by successive two-body transitions with exact conservation laws, and one-pion exchange produces the leading neutrons. Fourteen parameters are fitted to 1,254 points of the $π^\pm$, $K^\pm$, $p$, and $\bar{p}$ double-differential cross sections and eight neutron points. Under an error model that profiles the correlated systematic uncertainties, with a declared 5% model floor, the fit yields $χ^2 = 2263$ on 1248 degrees of freedom. On the same points, EPOS-LHC, UrQMD, and PYTHIA 8 at their published tunes give $χ^2$ values 4.2 to 14.4 times higher. The model needs no central source. The forward $K^+$ deficit, the forward $K^*(892)^0$ excess, and the flat $Λ$ $x_F$ distribution point to the momentum sharing at the vertex where the leading baryon turns into a hyperon. The $Ξ^-$ reaches 0.61 of the NA61/SHINE yield. The charged multiplicity of a heavy excited system grows linearly with its mass, faster than in $e^+e^-$ annihilation. The observables that distinguish a cascade from string and fireball models lie in the fragmentation region, where wide-acceptance fixed-target spectrometers can measure them.

title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
abstract: Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 φ)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer Rényi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. The modulation is predicted to be maximally strong and independent of the transverse momentum imbalance, $q$, from a dilute (BFKL) perspective, while it is considerably suppressed by saturation effects. In diffraction, we observe that the pair is always entangled and exhibits the same properties found in diffractive DIS. We explain how these properties follow directly from the exclusive and eikonal nature of the Pomeron exchange. We trace this behavior to a spin-density matrix of rank at most two with maximally mixed marginals. For this class of states, entanglement and Bell nonlocality coincide even when the state is mixed, while the explicit form of the light-front helicity amplitudes ensures that both persist in the whole phase space. We suggest accessing the spin correlations in unpolarized hadron collisions through the Collins and dihadron fragmentation functions. We point out that, in inclusive production, for massless quarks, suitably chosen double-Collins asymmetries provide promising entanglement witnesses.

title: Universal Critical Relations and Nonuniversal Scaling in Inverse-Square Ising Chains
abstract: For ferromagnetic Ising chains with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, the critical excess magnetization in a field inversely proportional to spin separation determines the connected correlation. Their slowly varying profile has finite logarithmic integral exactly when the ordered thermal slope is finite. For any finite nonnegative core, an exact tail gives inverse-logarithmic correlations and a square-root cusp. A relative correction $c/\log(n+e)$ with $c>1$ gives continuously varying logarithmic powers and a linear cusp. A lower bound on its disordered susceptibility excludes the usual Kosterlitz--Thouless law.

title: SU(2) Yang-Mills: Spectral Bounds, Vacuum Concentration, and Criteria for the Continuum Limit
abstract: A continuum mass-gap argument must preserve nonzero renormalized states and a positive spectral estimate while the spatial cutoff is removed and physical volume grows. We develop quantitative results that separate these requirements. Gauge reduction, reflection positivity and attributed strong-coupling estimates give physical-transfer bounds with nontrivial local sectors. At fixed spatial cutoff and positive coupling, we construct subsequential infinite-volume physical-time dynamics from local history correlations, with nonconstant gauge-invariant observables. For finite spatial boxes, explicit bounds apply to the entire physical vacuum complement; finite-matrix criteria include all omitted representations. Vacuum concentration gives extensive entropy bounds, quantitative fidelity obstructions for hard electric cutoffs, and necessary growth of retained representation spaces. A sharper local comparison yields complete bounds on fixed discarded-link sectors, while collective projection and Schur estimates isolate the additional input needed for a volume-uniform gap. The work also certifies a finite three-link conditioning functional through Wilson coupling 0.354, with its physical interpretation conditional on the stated block-comparison hypotheses. Exact blocking, corrected effective-potential theorems and a representation-by-representation two-dimensional benchmark clarify which approximations preserve the relevant observables. Published glueball measurements retain their original attribution; their reanalysis and the reproduced winding-channel and replica studies have explicitly statistical scope. Complete derivations and reproducible calculations support a set of certified benchmarks and continuum transfer criteria. A nontrivial four-dimensional spatial-cutoff construction and a positive spectral bound along it are not established; no exact continuum mass is asserted.

title: Real-time Electron Tagging by Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy in the PTOLEMY experiment
abstract: The PTOLEMY project aims at measuring the neutrino mass and, in the future, the Cosmic Neutrino Background from Tritium endpoint measurement. The Radio-Frequency (RF) Tracker is a sub-detector with the goal of measuring in real time the electrons by exploiting the Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy. In this work, an overview of the PTOLEMY project is given together with the design, simulation, construction and commissioning of the RF Tracker prototype: the Electron Trap. The measurements and data analysis of the Electron Trap are presented, establishing the primary path for the development of the RF Tracker.

title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we investigate finite-time boundary collisions and interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. We first prove that finite-time boundary collisions are impossible for arbitrary nonzero vortex circulations, without any restrictions on their signs or algebraic relations. The result excludes both simultaneous boundary collapse and individual vortex approaches to the boundary, without requiring convergence of the vortex trajectories. In contrast, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse by treating the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gröbli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.

title: Smooth Rigidity Near Extremal Horizons
abstract: The Einstein equations constrain the transverse Taylor series at a degenerate Killing horizon, but even complete knowledge of that series need not determine a smooth spacetime: a nonzero difference can vanish to every order at the horizon. We show that this ambiguity disappears when the limiting metric on the space of Killing orbits admits a spacelike graph over a compact horizon section. In dimensions $d\geq4$, smooth vacuum Einstein germs with the same marked transverse jets are then locally isometric on a two-sided neighborhood of the whole section. The proof combines a terminal wave-map gauge with energy estimates on the orbit cylinder and yields a finite weighted matching criterion. For unwarped horizons with positive-Einstein sections, a condition on the full Lichnerowicz spectrum reduces the smooth classification to parallel first transverse data. All such data have convergent multiwarped Einstein realizations, including examples whose sections have negative sectional-curvature directions. We also obtain a finite-regularity version for round sections. The continuation argument extends to four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory and gives smooth charged-Nariai rigidity. Finally, rotating Nariai data admit the required spacelike graph throughout the regular branch; an all-order tensor estimate yields smooth Kerr--de Sitter or rotating-Nariai rigidity for $a^2/r_0^2\leq1/8$, without assuming ambient axial symmetry.

title: Sitewise Generator Decomposition and Non-Equilibrium Steady States for Generalized Zero-Range Processes
abstract: In this paper we study the generalized zero-range processes considered in [20, 11, 12] with boundary driving. In these processes mass is moved between neighboring sites with rates depending only on the departure site. For a wide class of such models, the equilibrium stationary states are known to be of product form. We show that for such models, the boundary-driven generator can be decomposed into a sum of generators acting on single sites when integrating against (possibly inhomogeneous) products of the equilibrium marginals. We exploit this structure to derive new results for the harmonic models introduced in [15]. In particular, we prove that the propagation of mixture measures in [19] is still valid on graphs with asymmetric edges. On the chain geometry with asymmetric edges, we identify a class of models for which the NESS is given precisely by the NESS of the symmetric harmonic model on the chain. In addition to these results for harmonic models, we also present a new class of asymmetric models on the chain for which the NESS can be found explicitly and exhibits shock behavior. The large deviations for the density profile corresponding to these NESS are stated and proved.

title: The Lee-Yang property of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model
abstract: The Lieb-Sokal theorem provides a tool for establishing the Lee-Yang property of the partition function of a spin model if the corresponding single-spin partition function has this property and the interaction term in its Hamiltonian is of the form $-\sum J_{ij} S_iS_j$ with $J_{ij}\geq 0$. According to the result of this paper, the spin $S=1$ model with the Hamiltonian $-\sum (J_{ij} S_iS_j + K_{ij}S_i^2S_j^2) + \sum ΔS_i^2$ has the Lee-Yang property for all $K_{ij}\in \mathds{R}$ and $Δ>0$, whenever each $J_{ij}$ exceeds an explicitly computed bound $C(β, Δ, K_{ij})>0$, such that $C(β, Δ, K_{ij})\to + \infty$ as $β\to 0$. The latter suggests that the Lee-Yang property of this model may hold only for sufficiently low temperatures.

title: Machine learning assisted $ν/\barν$ discrimination in atmospheric neutrino events for CPV sensitivity in a 20-kton liquid scintillator detector
abstract: Atmospheric neutrinos span a broad range of energies and baselines, offering a complementary probe of leptonic CP violation. However, a JUNO-like liquid scintillator detector without a magnetic field cannot directly separate neutrino and antineutrino interactions, reducing CP violation sensitivity. This study investigates whether machine learning based statistical separation can improve CP violation sensitivity in a 20-kton detector. $ν_μ$ and $ν_e$ charged current events are generated with GENIE (using Honda flux) in a JUNO-like detector geometry and are reweighted using OscProb three flavor oscillation probabilities incorporating Earth matter effects and NuFIT parameters. Detector response is approximated by smearing lepton and hadronic energies, neutrino direction, and neutron multiplicity. Logistic regression, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers are trained on inelasticity, neutron multiplicity, and charged lepton energy, with XGBoost selected for the analysis. CP violation sensitivity is evaluated for a 200 kton-year exposure using a Poisson likelihood with systematic nuisance parameters and marginalization over five oscillation parameters within their respective $3σ$ ranges. XGBoost achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of approximately 0.83 for both flavor samples. Under the square root approximation, peak CP violation sensitivity improves from 1.49 $σ$ to 1.96 $σ$ for normal mass ordering and from 1.14 $σ$ to 1.61 $σ$ for inverted mass ordering. Machine learning based statistical neutrino-antineutrino separation can recover part of the CP violation sensitivity lost in charge blind detectors. These preliminary results motivate further studies incorporating validated detector response and systematic uncertainties.

title: Anomalous charge conjugation and parity in (2+1)-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics
abstract: We present a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly that involves $U(1)_Q$, $U(1)_F$, charge conjugation symmetry (acting only on $U(1)_Q$), and parity symmetry in $2+1$ dimensions. It is represented by a mutual Chern-Simons level $k_{QF}=\frac12 \,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z)$. Adopting the already established multi-charge anomaly sector, we explicitly provide the information that this response is $odd$ under $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ symmetries separately, but $even$ under combined $\mathsf{CP}$ symmetry. We also provide a global inflow representative and compute the equilibrium cross-charge response which includes $\partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4π\bmod 1/2π$. Using an analytic neutral-fluid example we show that this response is non-vanishing whereas the source-free hydrodynamic poles are invariant.

title: How to isolate charm production mechanisms using charm-anticharm rapidity and azimuthal angle differences
abstract: Charm production in hadronic collisions proceeds via many different processes, which makes it hard to calculate from first principles. Using PYTHIA simulations, we study correlations between charm and anticharm hadrons and show that hard-process charm, final-state splitting charm, and initial-state-shower charm populate markedly different regions of rapidity and azimuthal-angle difference. In particular, selections on the pair rapidity separation, $Δy$, can strongly enrich or suppress the near-side final-state splitting contribution and thereby provide experimental sensitivity to the different production processes. A comparison with existing LHCb $D^0\bar{D}^0$ correlation measurements from Run 1 motivates more differential studies using the substantially larger LHC data sets now available. Extending such measurements to heavy-ion collisions could further distinguish medium modifications of charm produced directly in the hard scattering from charm originating from a parent gluon, providing a new handle on the different interactions of heavy quarks and gluons with the quark-gluon plasma.

title: Holographic Einstein rings of a covariant quantum corrected AdS black hole
abstract: We investigate holographic Einstein rings in a covariant quantum corrected Schwarzschild--AdS$_4$ spacetime using a massless scalar probe. At fixed horizon radius $r_h$, the deformation parameter $ζ$ leaves the metric mass parameter, coordinate surface gravity, and photon sphere radius unchanged, while increasing the photon potential maximum and the asymptotic lapse coefficient $A=1+ζ^2$. The critical coordinate impact parameter approaches $A^{-1/2}$ for large black holes, whereas the corresponding incidence angle in the normalized boundary frame approaches $π/2$. Ray tracing and local WKB barrier data recover the same geometric scale. Quasinormal spectra computed with AdS boundary conditions provide a comparison at finite multipole number. These results separate the finite radius effect of the deformation from the change in boundary time normalization.

title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM
abstract: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the $V_2$ and $V_3$ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent $V_8$ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on $V_2$ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.

title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
abstract: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.

title: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
abstract: We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.

title: Gamma classes, central connection matrices, and tt* geometry
abstract: We review the gamma class of complex projective space, but from the point of view of topological-antitopological fusion. We deconstruct the central connection matrix which appears in the work of Dubrovin, Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani, and Cotti-Dubrovin-Guzzetti.

title: Observation of a strange $J^P=1^{-}$ resonance $K^{*}_1(1870)$ in $χ_{c1}\to K^+K^-η^{\prime}$ decays
abstract: A partial wave analysis of the process $ψ(2S)\to γχ_{c1}$, $χ_{c1}\to K^{+}K^{-}η^{\prime}$, with the $η^{\prime}$ meson reconstructed in the $π^+π^-γ$ and $π^+π^-η$ decay modes, is performed using a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3)\times10^{6}$ $ψ(2S)$ events collected with the BESIII detector. In the $Kη^{\prime}$ system, a resonant contribution with quantum numbers $J^{P}=1^{-}$ is observed for the first time and is denoted as the $K_1^*(1870)$ meson. Its statistical significance is $11.0σ$, and its mass and width are measured to be $M=(1869.0 \pm 14.6\pm 18.6$) MeV/$c^{2}$ and $Γ=(167.3 \pm 34.0\pm 24.2$) MeV, respectively. The branching fraction of the $χ_{c1}\to K^{\mp}K_1^*(1870)^{\pm}\to K^{+}K^{-}η^{\prime}$ decay chain is determined to be $(1.48 \pm 0.30\pm 0.33)\times10^{-5}$. The branching fraction of the $χ_{c1}\to K^{+}K^{-}η^{\prime}$ decay is measured to be $(7.90 \pm 0.48)\times10^{-4}$. Several intermediate scalar, vector, and tensor states are required to provide a good description of the data. These results provide new input for understanding strange-meson spectroscopy and investigating possible hybrid-state candidates.

title: Stanley Deser 19th March 1931 - 21st April 2023
abstract: Stanley Deser was Ancell Professor Emeritus at Brandeis University and Visiting Professor at the California Institute of Technology. He was a world-renowned theoretical physicist whose accomplishments include the Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) formulation of general relativity, supergravity with Zumino, the dynamics of flat space with Jackiw and 't Hooft and many other contributions to the quantum theory of gravity. In the 1980s he was instrumental in securing National Science Foundation approval of the LIGO gravitational wave experiment against much opposition. He was awarded the Einstein Medal in 2015 for important contributions to general relativity, in particular the development of the ADM formalism. Other awards include: The Dannie Heineman Prize 1994; Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences 1994; Honorary Member of the Torino Academy of Sciences 2001; Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences 1979, Fellow of the American Institute of Physics.

title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
abstract: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero Kähler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.

title: Parametrizations of the solutions of Love equations and their momenta
abstract: The Love equation is a paradigmatic example of a Fredholm integral equation of great interest in mathematics and physics, where its applications range from electrostatic problems to exactly solvable models for one-dimensional systems. In this work we propose a method to approximate the normalized solutions of Love equations of the first and second kind via a parametrization obtained by Hermite interpolation at Chebyshev nodes. Following the same approach, we also obtain approximations for the second, fourth and sixth momenta of the solution of the Love equations. We focus in particular on one-dimensional quantum gases described by the Lieb-Liniger and the Gaudin-Yang models. For these models, the solutions of Love equations correspond to the normalized densities of pseudorapidities. We show that remarkably accurate results can be obtained using the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation with a number of points as low as 17+2. In the case of the Lieb-Liniger model, we also propose a very accurate closed-form estimate of the dimensionless ground state energy valid for all values of the dimensionless interaction parameter incorporating known results for small and large couplings supplemented by the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation for intermediate couplings. As an application of this result, we compute the dimensionless local two-particle correlation function and the black soliton solutions of the Lieb-Liniger model.

title: Chaos Growth in a Generic 2D Hamiltonian System
abstract: We examine the geometric mechanism controlling the transition from local to global chaos in a generic 2D Hamiltonian system, the generalized Hénon-Heiles system. Using Poincaré sections and invariant manifolds, we show that the chaotic fraction grows through abrupt transitions associated with the destruction of invariant barriers. We introduce an index that gives the time required for the first penetration of a local chaotic domain into the global chaos. This index increases sharply and tends to infinity as a critical energy is approached. The set of lobes generates heteroclinic connections, while multiple unstable periodic orbits exhibit a global manifold structure characterised by repeated loops and lobes. However, in special chaotic cases close to the integrable Hénon-Heiles potential, where two asymptotic curves extend to infinity, the manifold topology differs qualitatively from the generic case, as the asymptotic curves no longer form closed structures surrounding the periodic orbits.

title: Precision Fragmentation Functions from Modern COMPASS SIDIS Data
abstract: We present a comparative account of three global determinations of collinear fragmentation functions (FFs) for charged pions, charged kaons, and unidentified charged hadrons. The HAPS-PiFF1.0, HAPS-KaFF1.0, and HAPS-hFF1.0 analyses combine single-inclusive $e^+e^-$ annihilation with charge-separated semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS), including the 2025 COMPASS proton-target measurements and the revised 2026 isoscalar-target results. Flexible neural-network parametrizations, Monte Carlo replicas, and NLO/NNLO perturbative setups are employed. The proton and isoscalar samples sharpen the flavor sensitivity of SIDIS, while gluon fragmentation remains comparatively weakly constrained. We discuss the effects of perturbative accuracy, the principal limitations, and prospects for future measurements.

title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
abstract: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.

title: The first-order phase transitions and gravitational waves from an effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models
abstract: First-order phase transitions in the early Universe can generate stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds in frequency bands targeted by proposed deci-Hz observatories. We study the gravitational-wave consequences of the right-handed gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2)_{R_1}\times SU(2)_{R_2}\to SU(2)_R$ in a Pati-Salam effective theory inspired by four-stack intersecting D6-brane models. The ultraviolet construction fixes the gauge structure and particle multiplicities, while the scalar masses and quartic couplings are treated as renormalized inputs below the supersymmetry-breaking scale. Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2Ω_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.

title: Exactly integrable field theory in $(2+1)$-dimensional space-time: the spectral equations
abstract: The primary object in quantum field theories is the one-step relativistic evolution operator. In this paper we consider the evolution operator defined on the auxiliary Kagomé lattice with the $q$-oscillator algebra of observables, the local ingredient of the evolution operator is the $q$-oscillator $R$-matrix of the Zamolodchikov tetrahedron equation. We construct explicitly the complete system of equations (which can be seen as a specific form of nested Bethe Ansatz equations) defining the spectrum of the evolution operator. This system of equations is valid for an arbitrary initial data (occupation numbers), and the thermodynamical limit is well defined for this system.

title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

title: Quark-level CPT violation in neutral-meson systems
abstract: This work investigates CPT and Lorentz breakdown in neutral-meson interferometry within the nonminimal Standard-Model Extension. Employing methods of chiral perturbation theory for mass dimension d=5, a connection between the quark-level and the meson effective pseudoscalar Lagrangian is established. The resulting phenomenological signatures in neutral-meson oscillations with particular focus on the detector geometry are explored. This analysis permits the interpretation of such CPT tests within the d=5 quark sector of the Standard-Model Extension. Existing data are used to extract first constraints on two coefficients and to estimate achievable sensitivity gains over published bounds of up to 18 orders of magnitude.

title: Kinematically Unrestricted Flat Space Scattering from AdS$_{d+1} \times$ S$^p$/CFT$_d$
abstract: We construct scattering states for scalar fields with generic kinematics from CFT operators in the flat space limit of AdS/CFT. The states can have momentum along the compact $S^p$ directions of $AdS_{d+1}\times S^p$, which is achieved by scaling to large R-symmetry charge and choosing a particular parameterization for the R-symmetry polarization. These states allow for the construction of an unrestricted S-matrix from the flat space limit of CFT correlation functions, which we check for various tree level interactions. We also describe a generalization of the Mellin space formalism which incorporates the compact momentum, and we discuss some possible implications for flat space holography.

title: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
abstract: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Bañados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.

title: Cylinder spectral curve and 1-cut Matrix model
abstract: For a random matrix, with eigenvalues in a one-body potential $V(x)$ and a 2-body interaction $R(x,x')$, it is known that the resolvent converges in the large $N$ limit to an analytic function in the complex plane minus cuts, called the spectral curve. In the 1-cut case, a two-sheeted neighborhood of the cut is a cylinder with two simple ramification points. We describe these spectral curve data by boundary integral operators and generalized cycles. Vice-versa, given a 2-branchpoints spectral curve in a cylinder, there exists a formal random matrix model that corresponds to it. The goal of this article is to show the method to recover a formal random matrix model, with its potential and 2-body interaction, from the geometry of the spectral curve.

title: Dynamical entropy on local causal horizons: the Einstein equation of state and canonical-energy flux
abstract: For a twist-free null hypersurface, the Hollands-Wald-Zhang (HWZ) representative $S_{\rm loc}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1-Vθ)dA$, local on each cross-section (cut), obeys an exact off-shell Raychaudhuri identity with no term linear in the expansion, so no final equilibrium cut is needed. Given an entropy density $1/4G$, the Unruh temperature $κ/2π$ of an approximate local boost, local equilibrium cuts, and stress-tensor conservation, equating the leading equilibrium change of $S_{\rm loc}$ to matter boost heat yields $R_{kk}=8πGT_{kk}$ for every null direction, hence the Einstein equation with undetermined cosmological constant, an equation of state in Jacobson's conditional sense. On a fixed caustic-free generator bundle with $dA=J\,dA_{\rm ref}$, the functional $S_{\rm L}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1+\ln J-Vθ)dA_{\rm ref}$ obeys an exact balance per reference cell with curvature, shear, and expansion terms all positive, so under null convergence $S_{\rm L}$ is nondecreasing for $V\geq0$ until the first caustic. Conversely, requiring this balance for positive affine parameter on every small bundle and null direction is equivalent to the Einstein equation, given conservation and the stated normalization. Cut-locality, positivity, and first-order HWZ normalization select the density $1+\ln J-Vθ$ uniquely within a two-function class. Both functionals depend on the affine origin; we give their shift laws, identify the anchoring-invariant content, and show the origin is physical data fixed by the equilibrium cut. Near equilibrium, $S_{\rm L}$ agrees with the HWZ dynamical entropy at first order, and the temperature-weighted change of its Hessian equals the HWZ modified canonical-energy flux for stationary-vacuum perturbations. At finite amplitude, $S_{\rm L}$ is only a monotone geometric functional; reading it as entropy requires a coarse-graining postulate, stated but not derived.

title: The random matrix hard edge --- applications, exact PDFs and large $N$ expansions
abstract: A hard edge of a Hermitian random matrix occurs when the eigenvalue density is strictly zero on one side of the edge, and nonzero on the other. Another possibility is that the eigenvalues occur in $\pm$ pairs, which creates a hard edge at the origin for the positive eigenvalues. Both review material and new results are presented for random matrix ensembles exhibiting a hard edge. The review material has two focuses: one is on applications of the random matrix hard edge, while the other is on exact eigenvalue probability density functions. The new results relate to the large $N$ expansion of correlation functions and conditioned gap probability generating functions with hard edge scaling for the Jacobi ensemble. For all even $β$ we are able to show that these quantities admit expansions in inverse even powers of the variable $N_{\rm hJ}':= N - 1/2 + (a + b + 1)/β$. For the $β=2$ Jacobi unitary ensemble, we can relate the leading (next leading) correction to the limit law to a particular second order (fourth order) differential operator applied to the latter. The analogous second order differential operator is found for $β=1,4$, leading then to its conjectured form for all $β>0$.

title: Thermodynamic, Optical, and Wave Signatures of Charged Letelier AdS Black Holes with PFDM and Quintessence
abstract: We study a four-dimensional charged Letelier--anti-de Sitter (AdS) black-hole metric containing a cloud of strings, a phenomenological perfect-fluid-dark-matter (PFDM) source, and a Kiselev-type quintessence term. We derive the curvature invariants, horizon temperature, entropy, electric potential, and horizon-based mass function, and analyze local thermal response and the associated extended-phase-space identities. A rectangular benchmark cycle gives $W=0.095000$ and $η\simeq15.39\%$ for the explicitly stated geometric-unit parameters; these values are model- and cycle-specific and are not presented as a universal efficiency enhancement. For geometric optics, we derive the photon-sphere condition, critical impact parameter, and finite-radius shadow angle. For a massless, minimally coupled scalar field, we obtain a radial-coordinate Helmholtz equation and identify frequency-dependent barriers, evanescent intervals, and candidate trapping regions; the eikonal barrier-top scale approaches the photon-sphere capture scale. Two qualifications delimit the interpretation. First, with the stated PFDM stress-tensor convention, $ρ_{\rm PFDM}=-β/(8πr^3)$, so positive $β$ describes a negative-density effective source. Second, the mass function follows from the horizon equation, but identifying it with a conserved asymptotic AdS mass requires a separate charge and boundary-normalization analysis. The potential-well analysis likewise does not determine complex quasinormal frequencies. We therefore present the results as a consistent, parameter-specific analysis of the adopted phenomenological geometry, while distinguishing algebraic thermodynamic identities from conclusions requiring asymptotic-charge or spectral calculations.

title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
abstract: Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. However, its power is limited by the small forward multiplicity in light-ion collisions. In this work, we study the effect of the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections on the symmetric cumulants in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV using EPOS4 with an ATLAS-like acceptance. Using the law of total covariance, the symmetric cumulant is separated into a selected part, which follows the differences between the $q_n$ classes, and a residual part within them. It is observed that in OO collisions the correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$ remain almost entirely within the $q_2$ classes, unlike in Pb--Pb collisions. Nevertheless, events with the smallest $q_2$ in central OO collisions show weaker correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$, which is attributed to $v_4$ approaching its linear response. In Pb--Pb collisions, the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections act separately on the two factors of the nonlinear coupling of $v_5$, which establishes a way to isolate them experimentally.

title: eAdS- embedded AdS, tensionless strings and contracted Carroll-Weyl symmetry
abstract: We adapt the Dirac conformal $d+2$ dimensional embedding construction to define a null string in $AdS_{d+1}$. Introducing an extra Stückelberg field $\varphi$, which is a scalar under $AdS$ and shifts under local scaling of embedding space, the model acquires a local scaling invariance. We refer to this string as the embedded anti-De Sitter, $eAdS$, null string. A very useful property of this new gauged formulation is that, unlike previous gauged actions in $AdS$ background, the local scaling symmetry commutes with the $so(d,2)$ symmetry of $AdS$. Interestingly, the $eAdS$ null string is the tensionless limit of a tensile string in embedding space and the same holds for its reduction to an intrinsic description of AdS. We display the symmetries and constraint algebras both in embedding space and directly in AdS.

title: Periodic Readout Induces a First-Order Generalization Transition in a Quantum Perceptron
abstract: Variational quantum classifiers can generate highly structured decision boundaries through the Fourier dependence of observable expectation values on circuit parameters. We show that expressivity can come at a sharp statistical cost, by considering a quantum perceptron whose readout is the simplest periodic classifier, namely a square-wave function of the weighted inputs, and determine its typical generalization in the thermodynamic limit using a teacher-student replica-symmetric theory. Above a critical oscillation frequency, increasing the training load induces a first-order transition from weakly to strongly teacher-aligned phases, resulting in a discontinuous improvement in generalization. At fixed load, however, increasing the frequency eventually drives the equilibrium generalization error to chance level, despite perfect classification of all the training examples. Thus, the same periodic structure that enhances random-label storage can delay the onset of learning. Our results expose a quantitative tradeoff between memorization and generalization generated purely by periodic readout, and provide a benchmark for understanding Fourier-rich variational quantum classifiers.

title: A novel Non-Homogeneous Local Representation of the Braid Group
abstract: We construct a non-homogeneous local representation of the braid group $B_n$ by tracking the labels of individual strands through successive crossings. Each generator acts through a $2\times2$ block whose position is determined by the crossing and whose coefficients depend on the ordered labels of the participating strands. Starting with the ansatz \[ M_{xy}=\begin{pmatrix}a_x&a_y\\ b_{xy}&c_{xy}\end{pmatrix}, \] for $n\geq3$, the cubic braid relations for arbitrary ordered triples of strands determine $c_{xy}=0$ and $b_{xy}=(1-a_x)/a_x$ in the nondegenerate branch. The moving-label rule leads to an explicit semidirect-product representation, for which we prove the Artin relations and use exact evaluations of the resulting symbolic matrices. In the special homogeneous specialization, where $a_x=a$ for every strand label $x$, the resulting matrix representation is diagonally equivalent to unreduced Burau. We prove that a non-homogeneous specialization of our representation detects Bigelow's explicit nontrivial $B_5$ Burau-kernel commutator. Thus the strand-dependent coefficients distinguish a nontrivial braid that is invisible to the classical Burau representation. This separation provides evidence that the non-homogeneous strand-tracking construction is a promising candidate for a faithful Burau-type representation.

title: Two-peak gravitational wave spectra from supercooled two-field phase transitions
abstract: We study the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum generated by supercooled first-order phase transitions in two-field conformal models. We construct three representative toy models that capture the essential features of these models, derive analytical criteria for the existence of two-step transitions, and show how the two-field dynamics generate a genuine two-peak GW spectrum. We identify regions of parameter space in which two-peak GW spectra are observable at LISA and the Einstein Telescope. By way of illustration, we apply our analysis to a realistic conformal dark SU(3) model.

title: Monodromy Defects and Bulk Renormalization Group Flows on the Fuzzy Sphere
abstract: A monodromy around a defect specifies a symmetry transformation, but the low energy properties of the defect depend on its interaction with bulk degrees of freedom and also itself. We study this dependence on the fuzzy sphere. Along an anisotropy flow, an $O(3)$ half-twist approaches the $O(2)$ half-twist when its twisted components stay light and disappears when they become massive. At large $N$, untwisted spectators give a positive correction to the defect entropy, fixed by the conformal weight of the free defect. The surviving $O(2)$ monodromy admits a relevant charged perturbation that pins the line. Pinning before or after the easy-plane bulk flow gives matching infrared junction data. A pin of the untwisted component survives only the opposite, easy-axis flow. Walls between opposite pinnings test the stability of the candidate ordered line. They are relevant on the pinned $O(2)$ monodromy lines studied and favoured to be relevant, with a smaller margin, on the ordinary $O(2)$ line, while the ordinary $O(3)$ and $O(4)$ walls lie close to marginality. We separate the wall dimension into a tilt stiffness and an angular shape, comparing them with a Ward identity, a two-loop expansion and a large-$N$ saddle. In the fully twisted large-$N$ model, winding weakens the condensate and lowers the wall dimension and the entropy released by pinning. The resulting entropy comparison permits disordering into the unpinned line wherever the leading wall estimate is relevant. Finally, we construct the regular half-twist on the fuzzy four-sphere as a starting point for analogous questions in five dimensions.

title: Variational Approach to the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon Equations of Motion for Extended Objects in General Relativity
abstract: The exact motion of a finite size object in curved spacetime is captured by the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations. They associate a unique worldline, momentum, and spin to that object and determine the evolution of such in terms of its fully independent multipole moments. We provide a thorough review of this theory and show how to build it directly via a manifestly gauge invariant variational principle well-suited for effective descriptions of relativistic compact objects. We discuss conditions under which the covariant spin supplementary condition can be enforced and identify the natural basis of curvature tensors conjugate to the object's multipole moments.

title: The Energy-Momentum Tensor of a Compact Object in General Relativity to all Multipole Orders
abstract: In effective field theory approaches to compact object motion in general relativity, spin and tidal effects are encoded by operators formed from the Riemann tensor and its derivatives. Many such operators contribute degenerately to observables, with a single one often affecting several multipole moments of the body. Using the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon formalism, we construct a natural basis of independent tensors which are each canonically conjugate to precisely one multipole. We find the novel exact distributional formula for the energy-momentum tensor of a compact object in terms of its reduced multipole moments and these tensors.

title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
abstract: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(δt)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $κ(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.

title: A new butterfly in the meadow: magnetic lattice graphs with a circulant vertex coupling
abstract: We analyze the spectrum of quantum square lattice graph exposed to a homogeneous magnetic field with a rational flux through plaquette, assuming all nontrivial cases of the vertex coupling which is circulant and scale-invariant, with a particular attention to those of them that give rise to a dynamics violating the time reversal invariance. Except for two cases with partially decoupled edges, the remaining twelve split into two spectral classes; the second one offers a hitherto unknown butterfly pattern.

title: Configurational Information and Hadron Spectroscopy in Holographic QCD
abstract: Based on the concepts of entropy and complexity, Configurational Information Measures (CIMs) are tools capable of extracting information regarding physical systems from their spatially localized energy density, determining properties such as stability limits and phase transitions. In this thesis, CIMs are employed to investigate hadron spectroscopy. By utilizing phenomenological AdS/QCD models in conjunction with CIMs, cataloged meson and baryon resonances are interpolated into structures analogous to Regge trajectories, from which analytical expressions are derived to estimate the masses of higher-order excited states. These estimates are compared with experimental data to search for possible correspondences that may elucidate the properties of particles that have been experimentally detected but remain unidentified. Using this CIM-based AdS/QCD hybrid method, this work analyzes light mesons within a dynamical model, strange vector kaons in a framework that accounts for constituent quark masses, and light-flavor baryons at finite temperature.

title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordström (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, arising as an exact solution of Einstein gravity. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. We provide several exact completions of this geometry with finite Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) mass. Focusing on the original logarithmic geometry, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Padé approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

title: A Geometric Theory for Nonequilibrium Transformer Dynamics
abstract: We develop a variational and geometric theory based on statistical physics for the joint evolution of Transformer attention and token representations at fixed model parameters. To this end, we introduce a free energy for the attention and model the evolution of the attention weights by its Fisher--Rao gradient flow. At fixed token representations, we prove that the softmax matrix is the unique free-energy minimiser and that every positive attention trajectory converges to it. For prescribed time-dependent representations, we show that the attention dynamics becomes linear after a change to logit variables. This result yields tracking bounds relative to the instantaneous softmax and sufficient conditions for attention to converge to a fixed matrix. Hamiltonian dynamics for the representations and their momenta are then coupled to the attention relaxation driven by the same energy. This coupling results in an energy-dissipation law. We also develop two alternative Hamiltonians incorporating the attention value map. We prove global well-posedness of the attention flow and all three coupled systems.

title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
abstract: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

title: A Beltrami Mode in Extreme Fractional Hydrodynamics under Stochastic Forcing
abstract: We construct an exact stochastic solution of the extreme order endpoint of adaptive fractional Navier Stokes (AFNS) hydrodynamics on the three-dimensional periodic torus. A helical Beltrami eigenfield reduces the nonlinear vector equation to a scalar Ornstein Uhlenbeck process when the white-in-time forcing is aligned with that eigenfield. The resulting invariant Gaussian law yields explicit formulas for the stationary energy, its fluctuations, temporal correlations, circulation, and helicity. Under the same forcing, the corresponding classical Navier Stokes mode has a stationary energy that diverges as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, while the Euler limit exhibits linear growth of the mean energy and has no invariant probability law. The construction isolates, without a cascade hypothesis, the statistical effect of the finite fractional dissipation retained at the extreme endpoint of AFNS.

title: Scalar-tensor reconstruction of coherent quantum black holes
abstract: We construct a scalar-tensor realisation of spherically symmetric black hole geometries that effectively arise from quantum coherent states characterised by a finite core and finite extension. We determine the non-minimal coupling to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian, kinetic coupling, and scalar potential and show that the kinetic term is positive only in finite domains. For fixed black hole mass, the boundaries of these domains provide a natural mechanism that relates the core size and spatial extension to the dynamics of the scalar-tensor realisation. We further show that the same geometry can also be obtained from a Horndeski action with derivative coupling and determine its domain of validity. Neither reconstruction includes the event horizon nor can it simultaneously reproduce arbitrarily large portions of the interior and exterior of the black hole, whose quantum origin therefore appears to remain partially outside the regime of applicability of semiclassical theories of gravity.

title: Mean Field Limit Towards Kinetic Equation with Repulsive Dirac-Delta Potential
abstract: A one-particle effective kinetic equation with repulsive Dirac-Delta potential in one dimension is rigorously derived from a moderate interacting second order particle system. It is proved that the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure and the solution of Vlasov equation converges to zero. A convergence rate is obtained by a combination of the estimates for particle trajectory and a smoothed version of modulated energy.

title: ERG, axions, and a PT-symmetric accelerating Universe
abstract: In conventional quantum mechanics, the Hamiltonian is required to be Hermitian, ensuring real energy eigenvalues. Certain non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also possess entirely real spectra when they are invariant under the combined action of parity ($\mathcal P$) and time reversal ($\mathcal T$). Such Hamiltonians are called unbroken parity--time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric. We conjecture that, in a string-inspired scenario, a repulsive phase of gravity may be due to a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric gravitational theory, characterised by anomalous Chern-Simons terms, coupled to axion fields. The conjecture is based on the behaviour of the chiral anomalous couplings of these axions to electromagnetic potentials. Within the Exact Renormalisation Group (ERG) framework in the modified local potential approximation, we argue that singularities in the ERG beta functions for such couplings may indicate an infrared phase transition. At the energy scales of these singularities, we conjecture that the field theory transitions from the Hermitian phase to a ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal T}$-- symmetric theory, of gravity, characterised by a repulsive Netwon's ``constant''. This may induce the acceleration observed in the Universe at late eras, without the need for a dark--energy component.

title: From many-body Schrödinger dynamics to magnetic Vlasov equation
abstract: We analyse the combined mean-field and semiclassical limit from the time-dependent Schrödinger dynamics of $N$ spinless fermions in a non-constant magnetic field to the magnetic Vlasov equation with scaling $\hbar = N^{-1/3}$. With the velocity-shifted coherent states and the induced magnetic Husimi measure, we derive an exact BBGKY hierarchy with a remainder of order $\hbar^{1/2-}$. The main result is the weak $L^1$ convergence of the $k$-particle magnetic Husimi measures to the $k$-copies of the solution to the magnetic Vlasov equation. Furthermore, the convergence holds in the Wasserstein distance $\mathbb{W}_2$ when the second moment of initial Husimi measure correspondingly converges.

title: Engineering a digital acoustic black hole
abstract: We show how to design and build an analogue black hole as a synchronous digital circuit. We define the sound speed, the flow and the horizon of such a circuit in terms of its own logic, and realise one on a field-programmable gate array, where the black hole is probed electrically with a signal generator and an oscilloscope. We measure the stability of the horizon, its causal cone, the ringdown and rotational superradiance. A single flipped bit inside the horizon leaks out by an amount that falls exponentially with depth. Digital circuits thus form a reconfigurable class of gravitational analogues and realise an analogue black hole as a cellular automaton.

title: Shallow-water black holes and lattice superradiance
abstract: Rotating black holes can amplify waves that scatter off them, a process known as superradiance that fluid analogues bring into the laboratory. Separating the horizon's role from dissipation in the surrounding fluid remains difficult. Here we realise a rotating analogue black hole in a lattice fluid: a shallow-water vortex whose horizon is set by a topographic sill, so that the only sink lies behind a supercritical layer that lets nothing out. We measure superradiance as energy extraction: the flux at the horizon is outward for co-rotating waves whose pattern rotates more slowly than the horizon, and inward for faster waves, counter-rotating waves and a non-rotating hole. A scan over three lattice viscosities separates the extraction at the horizon, which is inviscid, from that of the viscous fluid inside the corotation radius: well below the band edge the horizon is the absorber; near the edge the viscous share is half at the operating viscosity and vanishes at the lowest. A drain-anchored horizon, as in water-tank experiments, gives the same signs. Our analysis gives insight into the mechanism of superradiance and offers a cheap, flexible platform for designing analogue-gravity experiments.

title: Geometric classification of Noether invariants of the Time-Dependent damped Duffing Oscillator
abstract: We present a systematic geometric classification of the Noether point symmetries of time-dependent conformal Lagrangians of the form $L = A(t)\left(\frac{1}{2}g_{ij}\dot{x}^{i}\dot{x}^{j} - V(x)\right)$, whose Euler--Lagrange equations describe dynamical systems with time-dependent linear damping. The classification is carried out by coupling the temporal parameters of the conformal factor $A(t)$ with the homothetic algebra of the kinetic metric $g_{ij}$ through a set of compatibility and integrability conditions. The central result is a main theorem which determines the Noether generators, the associated gauge functions and the resulting invariants. The theorem splits naturally into two cases according to whether the quantity $D - 2ψ$ is non-zero or zero, with further subcases depending on whether the homothetic vectors are gradient or non-gradient. The theorem imposes no restrictions on $A(t)$, $g_{ij}$ or $V(x)$, and is therefore fully general and covariant. We apply the theorem to the time-dependent damped Duffing oscillator (DDO) in Euclidean space $E^{3}$ with $A(t) = e^{γt}$ and potential $V = \frac{1}{2}a\,r^{2} + \frac{% λ}{4}r^{4}$. For the damped harmonic oscillator ($λ= 0$) the theorem reproduces the classical Bateman invariant as a special case. For the anharmonic case we obtain a new exact time-dependent quadratic invariant, valid when the linear stiffness satisfies $a = 2γ^{2}/9$. Each invariant is verified explicitly by direct differentiation along the equations of motion. The new invariant provides a rare example of a global conservation law for a fully nonlinear dissipative system, and can be used for the integration and quantization of the DDO.

title: Non-Relativistic Supersymmetric Gauge Theories and Soliton Solutions
abstract: This paper investigates non-relativistic supersymmetric gauge theories obtained through null reduction, with particular focus on supersymmetric Abelian Higgs models and their soliton solutions. Starting from four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 1$ relativistic supersymmetric theories, we apply null reduction to derive Galilean-invariant non-relativistic theories in $2 + 1$ dimensions while preserving gauge symmetry and supersymmetry. The resulting symmetry structure is shown to correspond to the Bargmann extension of the super-Galilean algebra. We first analyze the massive supersymmetric Abelian Higgs model and show that, although it possesses nontrivial vacuum configurations, the mass term obstructs the existence of nontrivial BPS vortex solutions. We then study the massless supersymmetric Abelian Higgs model with multiple charged scalar fields, for which the BPS equations admit vortex-type soliton solutions under suitable charge and winding number conditions. The vacuum moduli space is identified as a weighted projective space, leading naturally to both integer and fractional vortex configurations. By imposing radial symmetry, we derive the corresponding vortex equations and examine their solutions analytically and numerically. Finally, we relate the vacuum structure of the model to the Ginzburg-Landau theory of superconductivity, highlighting how familiar superconducting behavior can emerge from a symmetry-preserving non-relativistic supersymmetric framework.

title: NuSTEC Review: Current Experimental and Theoretical Challenges of Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
abstract: The precise measurement of neutrino properties is among the highest priorities in fundamental particle physics, involving many experimental and theoretical efforts worldwide. Since the experiments rely on the interactions of neutrinos in the nuclear environment, the planned advances in the scope and precision of these experiments require a commensurate effort in understanding and modeling the hadronic and nuclear physics of these interactions, as incorporated in neutrino event generators. This modeling is essential to every phase of the experimental analyses, and the theoretical uncertainties play an important role in interpreting experimental results. In this Review of current challenges, we summarize the open questions in neutrino-nucleus interactions at GeV-scale energies, and discuss in detail the potential impacts of these unknowns on the measurement of neutrino properties, using the determination of oscillation parameters as a central example. After an Executive Summary and a concise Overview of the issues, we address how the neutrino event generators treat these challenges, how electron-nucleus interactions can help understanding these challenges and the important unanswered questions for each underlying physics process---from quasi-elastic to deep-inelastic scattering. Across every topic, we find that current challenges can be met only through active support and collaboration among specialists in strong interactions and electroweak physics, including theorists and experimentalists from both the nuclear and high-energy physics communities.

title: An RG perspective on the (un)naturalness of Starobinsky inflation
abstract: Starobinsky inflation is often regarded as a successful minimal model of the early universe, yet it relies on a large $R^2$-coupling, in apparent tension with the expectation that Wilson coefficients in a gravitational effective field theory are of the same order. We test this expectation with a first-principles renormalization group calculation. We use asymptotically safe gravity as a testing ground to define ultraviolet-complete renormalization group trajectories and to uniquely predict higher-order couplings in terms of the free parameters of the theory---the cosmological constant and the $R^2$-coupling in Planck units. Including higher-curvature operators up to the fourth order, we find that indeed the flow generates dimensionless couplings of comparable size in the ultraviolet, with the irrelevant couplings tied to the relevant ones by linear relations. However, at sub-Planckian energies a canonical-like scaling takes over, and the irrelevant couplings get suppressed by powers of the ratio between the inflationary and Planck scales. This hierarchy yields the suppression of higher-order operators needed for consistency with cosmological data, so that the $R^2$-dominated dynamics emerges as a natural low-energy approximation. At the same time, the higher-order terms required by fundamental physics induce small but calculable deviations from the Starobinsky predictions, which may be worth considering in light of the latest and future DESI and ACT results.

title: The Gribov problem on the horizon: A short guide to the Gribov-Zwanziger framework and its refinement
abstract: Gauge fixing in Yang-Mills theories encounters a non-perturbative obstruction: distinct gauge-equivalent configurations can satisfy the same gauge condition. These are the so-called Gribov copies and their existence challenges the global validity of the Faddeev-Popov prescription. Addressing this ambiguity motivates a framework that connects the geometry of gauge-field space to infrared dynamics. This mini-review introduces the Gribov problem in Euclidean Yang-Mills theories and traces the construction of the Gribov-Zwanziger action and its refinement through the introduction of dimension-two condensates. We discuss the resulting infrared propagators, their comparison to lattice results, and the role of BRST symmetry, before surveying selected applications and open questions.

title: Quantum Open Effective Field Theory: anomalous decoherence
abstract: We study decoherence of a scalar field coupled to ``anomalous'' environments with critical behavior with the Schwinger-Keldysh including the influence functional, and the quantum master equation (QME) up to second order in the coupling. The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation yields a Langevin equation and the Lindblad (QME) includes \emph{time dependent rates} allowing to study transient dynamics. We focus on three examples featuring non-Markov dynamics that cannot be described with S-matrix/Fermi's golden rule rates \textbf{i) Unparticle physics:} a conformal sector beyond the Standard Model at an infrared fixed point featuring correlation functions with anomalous scaling dimensions, \textbf{ii) Threshold and infrared enhancement:} when the mass shell of the field coincides with or is near to a kinematic threshold of the spectral density of the bath, \textbf{iii) Critical environments:} the bath is at a critical point, correlation functions scale with anomalous dimensions and long-wavelength fluctuations feature critical slowing down. In all cases the reduced density matrix undergoes decoherence in the energy basis of the probe, and off-diagonal matrix elements decay as $e^{-Φ(t)}$ with $Φ(t)>0 $ the \emph{decoherence function} and $Γ(t) = \dotΦ(t)$ the decoherence rate. In all cases we find that either transient or asymptotically $Φ(t) \propto t^{-μ}~;~ μ>0$ with $μ$, determined by the behavior of the spectral density at threshold and the anomalous scaling dimensions of the correlation functions, or $Φ(t) \propto \ln(t)$ for the infrared case. For a critical environment there is a new dynamical scaling exponent. A probe of frequency $ω_q$ is resonant with a \emph{critically slow} quasiparticle for $q_*\propto ω^{1/z}_q$ at which decoherence is strongly \emph{enhanced}.

title: Sensitivity to Sterile Neutrinos with Elastic Neutrino-Electron and Highly Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering in the DUNE Near Detector
abstract: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) is a next-generation neutrino experiment designed for precision measurements of long-baseline three-flavor neutrino oscillations. The DUNE Near Detector (ND) is also sensitive to short-baseline oscillations arising from mixing with an eV-scale sterile neutrino. In this paper, we present a sensitivity study for sterile-neutrino oscillations in the $3+1$ framework using three complementary event samples in the simulated DUNE ND: highly elastic $ν_μ$ charged-current (CC), highly elastic $ν_e$ CC, and neutrino-electron elastic-scattering ($ν+e$) events. These highly exclusive samples are chosen to reduce neutrino-interaction and flux uncertainties: the low-hadronic-energy CC selections enhance the correlation between reconstructed lepton energy and neutrino energy, while the precisely calculable $ν+e$ cross section provides an independent constraint on the neutrino flux. Residual interaction-model dependence remains in the CC samples. The statistical analysis considers $|U_{e4}|^2$, $|U_{\mu4}|^2$, $|U_{\tau4}|^2$, and $Δm^2$, with sensitivity results presented as fixed-$Δm^2$ slices for $|U_{\tau4}|^2=0$. The strongest sensitivity occurs for $4 \lesssim Δm^2 \lesssim 10~\mathrm{eV}^2$, where oscillations produce resolvable distortions of the reconstructed-energy spectra. For one year of on-axis forward-horn-current running, the 90\% confidence-level sensitivity reaches approximately $|U_{\mu4}|^2 \simeq 0.01$ and $|U_{e4}|^2 \simeq 0.015$, depending on the value of the other mixing parameter.

title: Evidence for quark+quark pairing in proton formation
abstract: The question of pairing between quarks inside baryons is addressed by calculating the fragmentation functions that describe production of nucleons (protons and neutrons) in high-energy collisions and comparing attendant predictions with phenomenological global fits to available data and directly with data on hadron multiplicities. The fragmentation functions are obtained from nucleon parton distribution functions using the Drell-Levy-Yan relation and subsequently solving a coupled set of pion, kaon, and nucleon jet cascade equations. Strong empirical evidence is found for the presence of diquark correlations. In comparison with global fits, $d$ (down) quark to proton fragmentation ($d\to p$) exhibits the clearest signals. The strongest evidence is found in comparisons with the momentum-dependent proton multiplicity distribution: FFs built from a proton wave function that contains diquark correlations deliver a $z$-profile that is fully consistent with available data, whereas that obtained from a no-pairing wave function is disfavoured by data at the $9σ$ level.

title: An exact unstable mode of self-similar Yang--Mills solutions in 5+1 dimensions
abstract: Self-similar solutions play an important role in the formation of singularities in the Yang--Mills equations. In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically in [1] that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $λ=5$. We explain this remarkable spectral property by an elementary construction of the corresponding eigenfunction.

title: Large-D approach to nearly critical holographic matter and Yang-Mills deconfinement
